77:    * intermediate values. */

79:       event->type == VS_INPUT_COMBO_PROGRESS)
80:     {
81:       uint8_t index;
82:       uint8_t i;

84:       for (i = 0, index = g_input_events.read;
85:            i < g_input_events.count;
86:            i++, index = (index + 1) % VS_INPUT_EVENT_QUEUE_SIZE)
87:         {
88:           if (g_input_events.event[index].type == event->type &&
89:               g_input_events.event[index].key == event->key)
90:             {
91:               g_input_events.event[index] = *event;
92:               pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_input_events.lock);
93:               return;
94:             }
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:   if (g_input_events.count == VS_INPUT_EVENT_QUEUE_SIZE)

108:   g_input_events.write =

689: {
690:   if (runtime->response_until_ms != 0 &&
691:       (int32_t)(runtime->response_until_ms - vs_app_now_ms()) <= 0)
692:     {
693:       runtime->response_until_ms = 0;
694:       runtime->response_pending_visible = false;

731:                               struct vs_runtime_s *runtime,

746:                    runtime->history_blank ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK :

748:                    true);

751:     vs_render(display, runtime);

754: static void vs_set_error(struct vs_runtime_s *runtime, int error,
755:                          enum vs_page_e return_page, bool retryable)
756: {
757:   runtime->error = error != 0 ? error : -EIO;
758:   runtime->error_return_page = return_page;
759:   runtime->error_retryable = retryable;
760:   if (runtime->network.error == runtime->error &&
761:       runtime->network.error_reason[0] != '\0')
762:     snprintf(runtime->error_reason, sizeof(runtime->error_reason), "%s",
763:              runtime->network.error_reason);
764:   else
765:     snprintf(runtime->error_reason, sizeof(runtime->error_reason), "%s (%d)",
766:              vs_errno_reason(runtime->error), runtime->error);
767:   runtime->page = VS_PAGE_ERROR;
768: }

770: static void vs_handle_app_event(struct vs_runtime_s *runtime,
771:                                 struct vs_network_s *network,
772:                                 const struct vs_app_event_s *event)
773: {
774:   if (event->type < VS_APP_EVENT_NETWORK_READY &&
775:       (event->request_id == 0 ||
776:        event->request_id != runtime->active_request_id))
777:     {
778:       return;
779:     }
780: 
781:   switch (event->type)
782:     {
783:       case VS_APP_EVENT_PHOTO_READY:
784:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_PHOTO_CAPTURE)
785:           {
786:             if (event->text[0] == '\0')
787:               {
788:                 vs_cancel_request(runtime);
789:                 vs_set_error_reason(runtime, -EBADMSG, VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK,
790:                                     false, "拍照未返回照片");
791:               }
792:             else
793:               runtime->page = VS_PAGE_VOICE_LISTENING;
794:           }
795:         break;
796: 
797:       case VS_APP_EVENT_PHOTO_FAILED:
798:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_PHOTO_CAPTURE)
799:           {
800:             vs_cancel_request(runtime);
801:             vs_set_error_reason(runtime, event->error, VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK,
802:                                 false, "拍照失败");
803:           }
804:         break;
805: 
806:       case VS_APP_EVENT_VOICE_REPLY:
807:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_VOICE_THINKING)
808:           {
809:             if (event->text[0] == '\0')
810:               {
811:                 vs_cancel_request(runtime);
812:                 vs_set_error_reason(runtime, -EBADMSG,
813:                                     runtime->photo_context ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK :
814:                                                              VS_PAGE_HISTORY, false,
815:                                     "AI未返回回答");
816:               }
817:             else
818:               {
819:                 snprintf(runtime->result_text, sizeof(runtime->result_text),
820:                          "%s", event->text);
821:                 runtime->page = VS_PAGE_VOICE_SPEAKING;
822:               }
823:           }
824:         break;
825: 
826:       case VS_APP_EVENT_VOICE_FAILED:
827:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_VOICE_LISTENING ||
828:             runtime->page == VS_PAGE_VOICE_THINKING)
829:           {
830:             vs_cancel_request(runtime);
831:             vs_set_error_reason(runtime, event->error,
832:                                 runtime->photo_context ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK :
833:                                                          VS_PAGE_HISTORY, false,
834:                                 "语音处理失败");
835:           }
836:         break;
837: 
838:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_STARTED:
839:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_STARTING)
840:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING;
841:         break;
842: 
843:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_START_FAILED:
844:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_STARTING)
845:           {
846:             vs_cancel_request(runtime);
847:             vs_set_error_reason(runtime, event->error,
848:                                 runtime->social_entry_return_page, false,
849:                                 "社交会话启动失败");
850:           }
851:         break;
852: 
853:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_ALERT:
854:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING ||
855:             runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ALERT)
856:           {
857:             runtime->emotion = event->emotion;
858:             runtime->emotion_color = event->color;
859:             snprintf(runtime->alert_text, sizeof(runtime->alert_text), "%s",
860:                      event->text);
861:             runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ALERT;
862:           }
863:         break;
864: 
865:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_ALERT_CLEARED:
866:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ALERT ||
867:             runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED)
868:           {
869:             runtime->emotion = VS_EMOTION_NONE;
870:             runtime->emotion_color = 0;
871:             runtime->alert_text[0] = '\0';
872:             if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ALERT)
873:               runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING;
874:           }
875:         break;
876: 
877:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_PAUSED:
878:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSING)
879:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED;
880:         break;
881: 
882:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_RESUMED:
883:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RESUMING)
884:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING;
885:         break;
886: 
887:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_PAUSE_FAILED:
888:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSING ||
889:             runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RESUMING)
890:           vs_set_error_reason(runtime, event->error, VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING,
891:                               false, "社交会话操作失败");
892:         break;
893: 
894:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_RESULT:
895:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_FINALIZING)
896:           {
897:             if (event->text[0] == '\0')
898:               {
899:                 vs_cancel_request(runtime);
900:                 vs_set_error_reason(runtime, -EBADMSG, VS_PAGE_HISTORY, false,
901:                                     "社交摘要为空");
902:               }
903:             else
904:               {
905:                 snprintf(runtime->result_text, sizeof(runtime->result_text),
906:                          "%s", event->text);
907:                 runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RESULT;
908:               }
909:           }
910:         break;
911: 
912:       case VS_APP_EVENT_SOCIAL_FINALIZE_FAILED:
913:         if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_FINALIZING)
914:           {
915:             vs_cancel_request(runtime);
916:             vs_set_error_reason(runtime, event->error, VS_PAGE_HISTORY, false,
917:                                 "社交记录整理失败");
918:           }
919:         break;
920: 
921:       case VS_APP_EVENT_NETWORK_READY:
922:         runtime->network_busy = false;
923:         if (network != NULL)
924:           (void)vs_network_get_status(network, &runtime->network);
925:         runtime->error = 0;
926:         runtime->error_retryable = false;
927:         runtime->page = runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP ? VS_PAGE_SOFTAP :
928:                         runtime->history_blank ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK :
929:                                                  VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
930:         runtime->progress = 0;
931:         break;
932: 
933:       case VS_APP_EVENT_NETWORK_FAILED:
934:         runtime->network_busy = false;
935:         if (network != NULL)
936:           (void)vs_network_get_status(network, &runtime->network);
937:         runtime->error_target_mode = runtime->network_target_mode;
938:         if (runtime->network_target_mode == VS_NET_STA)
939:           {
940:             /* Failing to join the configured Wi-Fi is an offline state, not a
941:              * product error.  Keep the photo home usable and wait for the next
942:              * explicit network attempt instead of showing an error page. */
943: 
944:             runtime->error = event->error;
945:             runtime->error_retryable = false;
946:             runtime->error_reason[0] = '\0';
947:             runtime->page = runtime->history_blank ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK :
948:                                                      VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
949:             printf("velasight: STA unavailable (%d), continuing offline\n",
950:                    event->error);
951:           }
952:         else
953:           {
954:             vs_set_error(runtime, event->error,
955:                          runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP ? VS_PAGE_SOFTAP :
956:                          runtime->history_blank ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK :
957:                                                   VS_PAGE_HISTORY,
958:                          network != NULL);
959:           }
960:         break;
961:     }
962: }

964: static void vs_handle_event(struct vs_display_s *display,
965:                             struct vs_runtime_s *runtime,
966:                             struct vs_network_s *network,
967:                             const struct vs_input_event_s *event)
968: {
969:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_PRESS)
970:     return;
971: 
972:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_COMBO_PROGRESS &&
973:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY || runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK ||
974:        (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING && !runtime->network_busy)))
975:     {
976:       runtime->page = VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING;
977:       runtime->progress = event->progress;
978:       return;
979:     }
980: 
981:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_COMBO_CANCEL &&
982:       runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING && !runtime->network_busy)
983:     {
984:       runtime->page = runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP ? VS_PAGE_SOFTAP :
985:                       runtime->history_blank ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK : VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
986:       runtime->progress = 0;
987:       return;
988:     }
989: 
990:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_PROGRESS && event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM &&
991:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY ||
992:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK ||
993:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER))
994:     {
995:       if (runtime->page != VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER)
996:         runtime->social_entry_return_page = runtime->page;
997:       runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER;
998:       runtime->progress = event->progress;
999:       return;
1000:     }
1001: 
1002:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_PROGRESS && event->key == VS_KEY_BACK &&
1003:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING ||
1004:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED ||
1005:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ALERT ||
1006:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING))
1007:     {
1008:       if (runtime->page != VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING)
1009:         runtime->social_exit_return_page = runtime->page;
1010:       runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING;
1011:       runtime->progress = event->progress;
1012:       return;
1013:     }
1014: 
1015:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_PROGRESS && event->key == VS_KEY_BACK &&
1016:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOFTAP ||
1017:        (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING &&
1018:         runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP && !runtime->network_busy)))
1019:     {
1020:       runtime->page = VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING;
1021:       runtime->progress = event->progress;
1022:       return;
1023:     }
1024: 
1025:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_CANCEL &&
1026:       runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER)
1027:     {
1028:       runtime->page = runtime->social_entry_return_page;
1029:       runtime->progress = 0;
1030:       return;
1031:     }
1032: 
1033:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_CANCEL &&
1034:       runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING)
1035:     {
1036:       runtime->page = runtime->social_exit_return_page;
1037:       runtime->progress = 0;
1038:       return;
1039:     }
1040: 
1041:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_CANCEL &&
1042:       runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING && !runtime->network_busy)
1043:     {
1044:       runtime->page = runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP ? VS_PAGE_SOFTAP :
1045:                       runtime->history_blank ? VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK : VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
1046:       runtime->progress = 0;
1047:       return;

349: int vs_network_open(struct vs_network_s **network)

351:   struct vs_network_s *n;

353:

393: int vs_network_request_mode(struct vs_network_s *network,
394:                             enum vs_net_mode_e mode)
395: {
396:   int ret;
397: 
398:   if (network == NULL)
399:     return -EINVAL;
400: 
401:   network->status.error = 0;
402:   network->status.error_reason[0] = '\0';
403:   network->status.state = VS_NET_SWITCHING;
404: 
405:   if (network->mode == VS_NET_AP && mode == VS_NET_STA)
406:     {
407:       ret = vs_network_stop_provisioning(network);
408:       if (ret < 0)
409:         {
410:           snprintf(network->status.error_reason,
411:                    sizeof(network->status.error_reason),
412:                    "AP provisioning stop (%d)", ret);
413:           network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
414:           network->status.error = ret;
415:           return ret;
416:         }
417: 
418:       /* stop() joins the listener, so no callback can race with this consume.
419:        * Apply a completed save even when manual exit won the UI race; discard
420:        * a failed save because the user explicitly chose to leave AP.
421:        */
422:       ret = vs_network_consume_saved(network, true);
423:       if (ret < 0 && ret != -ENOENT)
424:         {
425:           snprintf(network->status.error_reason,
426:                    sizeof(network->status.error_reason),
427:                    "保存WiFi配置 (%d)", ret);
428:           network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
429:           network->status.error = ret;
430:           return ret;
431:         }
432:     }
433: 
434:   ret = vs_network_stop_dhcp(network);
435:   if (ret < 0)
436:     {
437:       snprintf(network->status.error_reason,
438:                sizeof(network->status.error_reason), "DHCP停止 (%d)", ret);
439:       network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
440:       network->status.error = ret;
441:       return ret;
442:     }
443: 
444:   /* AP resources are gone before STA association begins.  If association or
445:    * DHCP then fails, the next network toggle must be able to enter AP again.
446:    */
447:   if (mode == VS_NET_STA)
448:     {
449:       network->mode = VS_NET_STA;
450:       network->status.mode = VS_NET_STA;
451:     }
452: 
453:   ret = mode == VS_NET_AP ? vs_network_apply_ap(network) :
454:                              vs_network_apply_sta(network);
455:     if (ret < 0)
456:       {
457:         if (network->status.error_reason[0] == '\0')
458:           snprintf(network->status.error_reason,
459:                    sizeof(network->status.error_reason),
460:                    "网络切换 (%d)", ret);
461:         network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
462:       network->status.error = ret;
463:     }
464: 
465:   return ret;
466: }

468: int vs_network_process_events(struct vs_network_s *network)
469: {
470:   int ret;
471: 
472:   if (network == NULL)
473:     return 0;
474: 
475:   ret = vs_network_consume_saved(network, false);
476:   if (ret == -ENOENT)
477:     return 0;
478: 
479:   if (ret < 0)
480:     {
481:       network->status.error = ret;
482:       network->status.state = VS_NET_AP_READY;
483:       return ret;
484:     }
485: 
486:   /* Keep AP and the provisioning listener alive after a save.  The saved STA
487:    * credentials are applied only when the user explicitly exits AP mode. */
488:   return 0;
489: }

497:   *status = network->status;

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_server.c
3:  *
4:  * The socket half of the provisioning entry.  Deliberately POSIX-only so the
5:  * accept loop, the ordering guarantee and one-shot mode can be exercised over
6:  * loopback on the host; the only thing left for the board is whether the
7:  * SoftAP and SD-NAND are actually there.
8:  *
9:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
10:  ****************************************************************************/
11: 
12: #include <arpa/inet.h>
13: #include <errno.h>
14: #include <netinet/in.h>
15: #include <poll.h>
16: #include <pthread.h>
17: #include <stdbool.h>
18: #include <stdio.h>
19: #include <string.h>
20: #include <sys/socket.h>
21: #include <unistd.h>
22: 
23: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
24: #include "vp_form.h"
25: #include "vp_http.h"
26: #include "vp_store.h"
27: 
28: #define VP_STATE_IDLE     0
29: #define VP_STATE_RUNNING  1
30: #define VP_STATE_FINISHED 2  /* the thread returned, still needs a join */
31: 
32: #define VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS  200
33: #define VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 1500
34: #define VP_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC 2
35: #define VP_STORE_PATH_MAX  192
36: #define VP_THREAD_STACK    8192
37: 
38: struct vp_server_s
39: {
40:   int       listenfd;
41:   int       clientfd;
42:   pthread_t thread;
43:   int       state;
44:   bool      stopping;
45:   bool      one_shot;
46:   char      store_path[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX];
47:   uint32_t  generation;
48:   velasight_prov_saved_cb_t on_saved;
49:   void     *cb_arg;
50: };
51: 
52: static struct vp_server_s g_server =
53: {
54:   .listenfd = -1,
55:   .clientfd = -1,
56:   .state    = VP_STATE_IDLE,
57: };
58: 
59: static pthread_mutex_t g_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
60: 
61: /* Request and response buffers are static because only one connection is
62:  * served at a time and 6KB of thread stack on this part is not free.
63:  */
64: 
65: static char g_request[VP_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS + VP_HTTP_MAX_BODY + 1];
66: static char g_response[VP_HTTP_RESPONSE_MAX];
67: 
68: static int vp_write_all(int fd, const char *data, size_t len)
69: {
70:   size_t sent = 0;
71: 
72:   while (sent < len)
73:     {
74:       ssize_t n = write(fd, data + sent, len - sent);
75: 
76:       if (n < 0)
77:         {
78:           if (errno == EINTR)
79:             {
80:               continue;
81:             }
82: 
83:           return -errno;
84:         }
85: 
86:       if (n == 0)
87:         {
88:           return -EPIPE;
89:         }
90: 
91:       sent += (size_t)n;
92:     }
93: 
94:   return 0;
95: }
96: 
97: /****************************************************************************
98:  * Name: vp_read_request
99:  *
100:  * Description:
101:  *   Read until the headers plus the declared body have arrived, the cap is
102:  *   reached or the deadline passes.  Returns the total length, or negative on
103:  *   error.  A client that opens a connection and says nothing costs one
104:  *   timeout, not the service.
105:  *
106:  ****************************************************************************/
107: 
108: static int vp_read_request(int fd, struct vp_http_request_s *req)
109: {
110:   size_t total = 0;
111:   int waited = 0;
112: 
113:   for (; ; )
114:     {
115:       struct pollfd pfd;
116:       ssize_t n;
117:       int ret;
118: 
119:       ret = vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req);
120:       if (ret == 0)
121:         {
122:           if (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
123:               total >= req->header_len + req->content_length)
124:             {
125:               return (int)total;
126:             }
127:         }
128:       else if (ret != -EAGAIN)
129:         {
130:           return ret;
131:         }
132: 
133:       if (total >= sizeof(g_request) - 1)
134:         {
135:           return -E2BIG;
136:         }
137: 
138:       pfd.fd = fd;
139:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
140:       pfd.revents = 0;
141:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
142:       if (ret < 0)
143:         {
144:           if (errno == EINTR)
145:             {
146:               continue;
147:             }
148: 
149:           return -errno;
150:         }
151: 
152:       if (ret == 0)
153:         {
154:           waited += VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS;
155:           if (waited >= VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)
156:             {
157:               return -ETIMEDOUT;
158:             }
159: 
160:           continue;
161:         }
162: 
163:       n = read(fd, g_request + total, sizeof(g_request) - 1 - total);
164:       if (n < 0)
165:         {
166:           if (errno == EINTR)
167:             {
168:               continue;
169:             }
170: 
171:           return -errno;
172:         }
173: 
174:       if (n == 0)
175:         {
176:           /* Peer closed.  Whatever arrived is all there will be, so let the
177:            * parser decide between "incomplete" and "answerable".
178:            */
179: 
180:           if (vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req) == 0 &&
181:               (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
182:                total >= req->header_len + req->content_length))
183:             {
184:               return (int)total;
185:             }
186: 
187:           return -ECONNRESET;
188:         }
189: 
190:       total += (size_t)n;
191:     }
192: }
193: 
194: /****************************************************************************
195:  * Name: vp_handle
196:  *
197:  * Description:
198:  *   Serve one connection.  Sets *saved when credentials were persisted and
199:  *   *save_status to 0 or the negative errno of a failed save, so the caller can
200:  *   notify the application only after the socket is gone.
201:  *
202:  ****************************************************************************/
203: 
204: static void vp_handle(int fd, bool *saved, int *save_status,
205:                       uint32_t *generation)
206: {
207:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
208:   struct vp_http_request_s req;
209:   size_t len = 0;
210:   int ret;
211: 
212:   *saved = false;
213:   *save_status = 0;
214: 
215:   ret = vp_read_request(fd, &req);
216:   if (ret < 0)
217:     {
218:       if (ret == -E2BIG)
219:         {
220:           len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 431,
221:                                     "请求过大。");
222:         }
223:       else
224:         {
225:           /* Nothing usable arrived; answering a client that already gave up
226:            * is not worth a second syscall.
227:            */
228: 
229:           return;
230:         }
231:     }
232:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_PAGE)
233:     {
234:        {
235:          struct velasight_prov_credentials_s current;
236:          const char *ssid = NULL;
237: 
238:          if (velasight_provisioning_load(&current) == 0)
239:            ssid = current.ssid;
240:          len = vp_http_form_page_with_ssid(g_response, sizeof(g_response),
241:                                            NULL, ssid);
242:        }
243:     }
244:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_REJECT)
245:     {
246:       len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), req.status,
247:                                req.status == 404 ? "页面不存在。" :
248:                                req.status == 405 ? "不支持该请求方法。" :
249:                                req.status == 413 ? "提交内容过大。" :
250:                                req.status == 415 ? "提交格式不受支持。" :
251:                                req.status == 411 ? "缺少 Content-Length。" :
252:                                                    "请求无法解析。");
253:     }
254:   else
255:     {
256:       memset(&cred, 0, sizeof(cred));
257:       ret = vp_form_parse(g_request + req.header_len, req.content_length,
258:                           &cred);
259:       if (ret < 0)
260:         {
261:           /* No detail about which field failed and no echo of what was typed:
262:            * the notice has to be useful to the person at the phone without
263:            * repeating a passphrase back over an open network.
264:            */
265: 
266:            {
267:              struct velasight_prov_credentials_s current;
268:              const char *ssid = NULL;
269: 
270:              if (velasight_provisioning_load(&current) == 0)
271:                ssid = current.ssid;
272:              len = vp_http_form_page_with_ssid(
273:                  g_response, sizeof(g_response),
274:                  "SSID 需 1-32 字节，密码需留空或 8-63 字节，"
275:                  "API key 需为可打印字符，请检查后重试。", ssid);
276:            }
277:           if (len > 0)
278:             {
279:               /* Reuse the form page body but answer 400, so a client that
280:                * checks the status still learns the submit failed.
281:                */
282: 
283:               len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 400,
284:                                         "SSID 需 1-32 字节，密码需留空或 "
285:                                         "8-63 字节。");
286:             }
287:         }
288:         else
289:           {
290:             struct velasight_prov_credentials_s previous;
291: 
292:             /* The API key field is intentionally never pre-filled in HTML.
293:              * An ordinary Wi-Fi-only resubmit must not erase the existing key. */
294:             if (cred.api_key[0] == '\0' &&
295:                 velasight_provisioning_load(&previous) == 0)
296:               {
297:                 snprintf(cred.api_key, sizeof(cred.api_key), "%s",
298:                          previous.api_key);
299:               }
300: 
301:             cred.generation = vp_store_next_generation(g_server.store_path);
302:           ret = vp_store_save(g_server.store_path, &cred);
303:           if (ret < 0)
304:             {
305:               *saved = false;
306:               *save_status = ret;
307:               len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 500,
308:                                         "写入持久存储失败，凭据未保存。");
309:             }
310:           else
311:             {
312:               *saved = true;
313:               *save_status = 0;
314:               *generation = cred.generation;
315:               len = vp_http_saved_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response),
316:                                        cred.ssid, cred.generation,
317:                                        cred.open_network);
318:             }
319:         }
320:     }
321: 
322:   if (len > 0)
323:     {
324:       ret = vp_write_all(fd, g_response, len);
325:       if (ret < 0)
326:         {
327:           /* Keep AP mode available when the phone disconnected before it
328:            * received the result page.  The record itself was already saved.
329:            */
330:           if (*saved)
331:             {
332:               *saved = false;
333:             }
334:           *save_status = ret;
335:         }
336:     }
337: }
338: 
339: static void *vp_thread(void *arg)
340: {
341:   (void)arg;
342: 
343:   for (; ; )
344:     {
345:       struct pollfd pfd;
346:       uint32_t generation = 0;
347:       int save_status = 0;
348:       bool saved = false;
349:       bool stopping;
350:       int fd;
351:       int ret;
352: 
353:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
354:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
355:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
356:       if (stopping)
357:         {
358:           break;
359:         }
360: 
361:       pfd.fd = g_server.listenfd;
362:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
363:       pfd.revents = 0;
364: 
365:       /* Polling rather than blocking in accept(): stop() then needs no signal
366:        * and no socket shutdown trick that may or may not wake accept on a
367:        * given stack.
368:        *
369:        * This requires CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG on NuttX, which the Kconfig
370:        * depends on.  Without it TCP_BACKLOG events never fire, POLLIN on a
371:        * listening socket is unreachable, and accept() blocks with no timeout
372:        * at all -- measured on the board as a service that reported
373:        * "listening" and then answered nothing.
374:        */
375: 
376:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
377:       if (ret < 0)
378:         {
379:           if (errno == EINTR)
380:             {
381:               continue;
382:             }
383: 
384:           break;
385:         }
386: 
387:       if (ret == 0)
388:         {
389:           continue;
390:         }
391: 
392:       fd = accept(g_server.listenfd, NULL, NULL);
393:       if (fd < 0)
394:         {
395:           if (errno == EINTR || errno == ECONNABORTED)
396:             {
397:               continue;
398:             }
399: 
400:           break;
401:         }
402: 
403:       {
404:         struct timeval tv;
405: 
406:         tv.tv_sec = VP_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC;
407:         tv.tv_usec = 0;
408:         (void)setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &tv, sizeof(tv));
409:         (void)setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDTIMEO, &tv, sizeof(tv));
410:       }
411: 
412:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
413:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
414:       if (!stopping)
415:         {
416:           g_server.clientfd = fd;
417:         }
418:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
419:       if (stopping)
420:         {
421:           shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR);
422:           close(fd);
423:           break;
424:         }
425: 
426:       printf("provision_web: accepted client\n");
427:       vp_handle(fd, &saved, &save_status, &generation);
428: 
429:        /* Close before notifying.  The application may leave SoftAP from the
430:         * callback, and doing that with the response still in flight is what
431:         * makes a successful save look like a failed submit on the phone.
432:        */
433: 
434:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
435:       if (g_server.clientfd == fd)
436:         {
437:           g_server.clientfd = -1;
438:         }
439:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
440:       shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR);
441:       close(fd);
442: 
443:       if (saved)
444:         {
445:           pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
446:           g_server.generation = generation;

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_http.h
3:  *
4:  * The smallest HTTP surface that can serve one form and accept one submit.
5:  * Everything it does not recognise is refused with a status rather than
6:  * tolerated: this listener sits on an open SoftAP, so "be liberal in what you
7:  * accept" buys nothing and costs attack surface.
8:  *
9:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
10:  ****************************************************************************/
11: 
12: #ifndef __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_HTTP_H
13: #define __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_HTTP_H
14: 
15: #include <stdbool.h>
16: #include <stddef.h>
17: #include <stdint.h>
18: 
19: /* Request headers and body caps.  A provisioning form needs a few hundred
20:  * bytes; anything larger is a mistake or a probe.
21:  */
22: 
23: #define VP_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS 2048
24: #define VP_HTTP_MAX_BODY    1024
25: 
26: /* Enough for the form page plus the largest status page. */
27: 
28: #define VP_HTTP_RESPONSE_MAX 4096
29: 
30: enum vp_http_action_e
31: {
32:   VP_HTTP_ACTION_PAGE = 0, /* GET / -- serve the form */
33:   VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE,     /* POST /save -- body is a form submit */
34:   VP_HTTP_ACTION_REJECT    /* answer with .status and close */
35: };
36: 
37: struct vp_http_request_s
38: {
39:   enum vp_http_action_e action;
40:   int                   status;         /* Only meaningful when REJECT */
41:   size_t                header_len;     /* Includes the blank line */
42:   size_t                content_length; /* 0 unless SAVE */
43: };
44: 
45: /****************************************************************************
46:  * Name: vp_http_parse
47:  *
48:  * Description:
49:  *   Parse whatever has arrived so far.  Returns -EAGAIN while the headers are
50:  *   incomplete and 0 once a decision has been made, with action saying what
51:  *   to do.  Rejections carry the status to answer with:
52:  *
53:  *     405  a method other than GET or POST
54:  *     404  an unknown path
55:  *     411  POST without Content-Length
56:  *     413  a body over VP_HTTP_MAX_BODY
57:  *     415  a submit that is not form-urlencoded
58:  *     431  headers over VP_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS
59:  *     400  anything malformed, including chunked bodies
60:  *
61:  ****************************************************************************/
62: 
63: int vp_http_parse(const char *buf, size_t len,
64:                   struct vp_http_request_s *req);
65: 
66: /****************************************************************************
67:  * Name: vp_html_escape
68:  *
69:  * Description:
70:  *   Escape &, <, >, " and ' for insertion into element text or an attribute.
71:  *   Returns the escaped length or -E2BIG.  The SSID comes from the network,
72:  *   so it is untrusted even though it is short.
73:  *
74:  ****************************************************************************/
75: 
76: int vp_html_escape(const char *in, char *out, size_t outlen);
77: 
78: /* Response builders.  Each returns the number of bytes written, or 0 when the
79:  * buffer is too small.  No password is ever part of a response body, which
80:  * the host tests assert directly rather than trust.
81:  */
82: 
83: size_t vp_http_form_page(char *buf, size_t buflen, const char *notice);
84: 
85: size_t vp_http_form_page_with_ssid(char *buf, size_t buflen,
86:                                    const char *notice,
87:                                    const char *current_ssid);
88: 
89: size_t vp_http_saved_page(char *buf, size_t buflen, const char *ssid,
90:                           uint32_t generation, bool open_network);
91: 
92: size_t vp_http_status_page(char *buf, size_t buflen, int status,
93:                            const char *message);
94: 
95: #endif /* __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_HTTP_H */

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_form.h
3:  *
4:  * application/x-www-form-urlencoded decoding and credential validation.  No
5:  * NuttX includes on purpose: every edge case here (a truncated %, a duplicate
6:  * field, a 64-byte passphrase) is provoked by the host tests in milliseconds
7:  * instead of by retyping a form on a phone.
8:  *
9:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
10:  ****************************************************************************/
11: 
12: #ifndef __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_FORM_H
13: #define __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_FORM_H
14: 
15: #include <stddef.h>
16: 
17: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
18: 
19: /* A provisioning form has two fields.  The cap exists so a body full of
20:  * unknown keys cannot keep the parser busy; it is not a promise about which
21:  * keys are understood.
22:  */
23: 
24: #define VP_FORM_MAX_FIELDS 16
25: 
26: /****************************************************************************
27:  * Name: vp_url_decode
28:  *
29:  * Description:
30:  *   Decode one form component.  '+' becomes a space, %xx becomes the byte.
31:  *   Returns the decoded length, -EINVAL for a malformed escape or an embedded
32:  *   NUL, or -E2BIG when the result does not fit with its terminator.
33:  *
34:  ****************************************************************************/
35: 
36: int vp_url_decode(const char *src, size_t srclen, char *out, size_t outlen);
37: 
38: /****************************************************************************
39:  * Name: vp_credentials_validate
40:  *
41:  * Description:
42:  *   SSID must be 1..32 bytes without control characters.  The password is
43:  *   either empty, meaning an open network, or 8..63 printable ASCII bytes,
44:  *   which is what WPA2 accepts.  Returns 0 or -EINVAL.
45:  *
46:  ****************************************************************************/
47: 
48: int vp_credentials_validate(
49:     const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
50: 
51: /****************************************************************************
52:  * Name: vp_form_parse
53:  *
54:  * Description:
55:  *   Parse a submitted body into credentials.  ssid is required; a missing
56:  *   password field means an open network.  A repeated ssid or password is
57:  *   rejected rather than resolved, because either choice would be a guess.
58:  *   Unknown fields are ignored.  Returns 0, -EINVAL, or -E2BIG.
59:  *
60:  *   generation is left untouched: the store owns it.
61:  *
62:  ****************************************************************************/
63: 
64: int vp_form_parse(const char *body, size_t bodylen,
65:                   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
66: 
67: #endif /* __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_FORM_H */

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_store.h
3:  *
4:  * The persisted record and its atomic replacement.  Fixed size, versioned,
5:  * length-checked and CRC-protected, because a half-written credential file on
6:  * a VFAT volume that loses power mid-write is otherwise indistinguishable
7:  * from a valid one.
8:  *
9:  * The passphrase and API key are stored in the clear.  VFAT has no permission model worth
10:  * relying on and this chip has no confirmed device key, so pretending to
11:  * encrypt would only hide the exposure.  What is controlled instead: it is
12:  * never logged, never echoed back over HTTP, and only read through the public
13:  * API.  Physical access to the SD-NAND reveals it.
14:  *
15:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
16:  ****************************************************************************/
17: 
18: #ifndef __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_STORE_H
19: #define __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_STORE_H
20: 
21: #include <stddef.h>
22: #include <stdint.h>
23: 
24: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
25: 
26: /* Layout, little-endian:
27:  *
28:  *   0   4   magic "VSWP"
29:  *   4   2   version, currently 2
30:  *   6   2   flags, bit0 = open network
31:  *   8   4   generation
32:  *   12  1   ssid_len, 1..32
33:  *   13  1   psk_len, 0 or 8..63
34:  *   14  32  ssid, zero padded
35:  *   46  63  password, zero padded
36:  *   109 512 API key, zero padded
37:  *   621 1   reserved, must be zero
38:  *   622 4   CRC32 of bytes 0..621
39:  */
40: 
41: #define VP_RECORD_SIZE    626
42: #define VP_RECORD_VERSION 2
43: #define VP_RECORD_MAGIC   "VSWP"
44: 
45: #define VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN 0x0001u
46: 
47: uint32_t vp_crc32(const void *data, size_t len);
48: 
49: /****************************************************************************
50:  * Name: vp_record_encode / vp_record_decode
51:  *
52:  * Description:
53:  *   Serialize and parse the record.  encode returns VP_RECORD_SIZE, -EINVAL
54:  *   for credentials that do not validate, or -E2BIG for a short buffer.
55:  *   decode returns 0 or -EBADMSG; it checks the magic, the version, both
56:  *   lengths, that the open flag agrees with psk_len, the reserved byte and
57:  *   the CRC.  A record that fails any of those is corrupt, not repairable.
58:  *
59:  ****************************************************************************/
60: 
61: int vp_record_encode(uint8_t *buf, size_t buflen,
62:                      const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
63: 
64: int vp_record_decode(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len,
65:                      struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
66: 
67: /****************************************************************************
68:  * Name: vp_store_temp_path
69:  *
70:  * Description:
71:  *   The scratch file used by vp_store_save(), placed beside the record.
72:  *
73:  *   It is a fixed name rather than "<path>.tmp" because the SD-NAND is VFAT
74:  *   without long-name support: "wifi.bin.tmp" has two dots and every
75:  *   component must fit 8.3, so the obvious derivation is rejected with
76:  *   -EINVAL by the filesystem.  One save runs at a time, so a fixed name
77:  *   costs nothing.
78:  *
79:  *   Returns 0, or -E2BIG when the buffer is too small.
80:  *
81:  ****************************************************************************/
82: 
83: int vp_store_temp_path(const char *path, char *buf, size_t buflen);
84: 
85: /****************************************************************************
86:  * Name: vp_store_save
87:  *
88:  * Description:
89:  *   Write the record to the scratch file, flush it, fsync it, then rename it
90:  *   over the target, so a reader sees a complete record rather than a
91:  *   half-written one.  Creates the parent directory when it is missing.  On
92:  *   failure a complete scratch file is retained for load-time recovery.
93:  *   Returns 0 or a negative errno.
94:  *
95:  *   On VFAT the rename is not a single atomic step -- NuttX's VFS unlinks an
96:  *   existing target first, and FAT's own rename refuses to overwrite -- so
97:  *   there is a brief window in which the record is absent.  That is the
98:  *   strongest guarantee this filesystem offers; a reader in that window gets
99:  *   -ENOENT, never a truncated record, because the CRC would catch it.
100:  *
101:  ****************************************************************************/
102: 
103: int vp_store_save(const char *path,
104:                   const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
105: 
106: /****************************************************************************
107:  * Name: vp_store_load
108:  *
109:  * Description:
110:  *   Read and validate the record.  Returns 0, -ENOENT, -EBADMSG for a corrupt
111:  *   or wrong-sized file, or a negative errno.
112:  *   If the final path is absent but a complete scratch record exists, load
113:  *   validates and promotes that record before returning it.
114:  *
115:  ****************************************************************************/
116: 
117: int vp_store_load(const char *path,
118:                   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
119: 
120: /****************************************************************************
121:  * Name: vp_store_next_generation
122:  *
123:  * Description:
124:  *   The generation to stamp on the next save: one past whatever is stored, or
125:  *   1 when nothing readable is there.  A corrupt record does not reset the
126:  *   counter to a value already used, it simply starts over at 1, which is the
127:  *   only honest answer when the old value is unreadable.
128:  *
129:  ****************************************************************************/
130: 
131: uint32_t vp_store_next_generation(const char *path);

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/include/velasight_provisioning.h
3:  *
4:  * AP-mode provisioning web entry.  The application switches the radio into
5:  * SoftAP itself, calls velasight_provisioning_start(), and gets told when a
6:  * phone has submitted credentials.  This service never touches the Wi-Fi
7:  * role: it does not associate, does not run wapi, does not start DHCPD and
8:  * does not switch back to STA.  Owning both the HTTP page and the radio would
9:  * make it impossible for the application to decide when the network may drop.
10:  *
11:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
12:  ****************************************************************************/
13: 
14: #ifndef __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_INCLUDE_VELASIGHT_PROVISIONING_H
15: #define __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_INCLUDE_VELASIGHT_PROVISIONING_H
16: 
17: #include <stdbool.h>
18: #include <stddef.h>
19: #include <stdint.h>
20: 
21: #ifdef __cplusplus
22: extern "C"
23: {
24: #endif
25: 
26: /* IEEE 802.11 SSID length, and the WPA2 passphrase range.  An empty password
27:  * means an open network, which is the only reason 0 is legal.
28:  */
29: 
30: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX 32
31: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MIN  8
32: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX  63
33: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_API_KEY_MAX 512
34: 
35: /* Where the record lives when the caller passes no path.  On SD-NAND, so it
36:  * survives a reset; /mnt itself is pseudo-filesystem and /mnt/ram is a PSRAM
37:  * ramdisk, neither of which would.
38:  *
39:  * Every component fits 8.3 because that SD-NAND is VFAT without long-name
40:  * support (CONFIG_FAT_LFN is not set). This single file contains Wi-Fi
41:  * credentials and the MiMo API key; deprecated KVDB is not used.
42:  */
43: 
44: #ifndef CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE
45: #  define CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE "/mnt/sdnand/prov/vela.cfg"
46: #endif
47: 
48: #ifndef CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT
49: #  define CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT 80
50: #endif
51: 
52: struct velasight_prov_credentials_s
53: {
54:   char     ssid[VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX + 1];
55:   char     password[VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX + 1];
56:   char     api_key[VELASIGHT_PROV_API_KEY_MAX + 1];
57:   uint32_t generation;   /* Monotonic save counter, first save is 1 */
58:   bool     open_network; /* Password is empty */
59: };
60: 
61: /* Called after the success page has been written and the connection closed,
62:  * never before.  The application may leave SoftAP from here, but keeping the
63:  * listener alive is also valid and lets the user submit another record. Doing
64:  * radio work mid-response is what makes a phone show "submit failed" for a
65:  * save that actually happened.
66:  *
67:  * status is 0 on success or a negative errno.  Credentials are deliberately
68:  * absent -- read them with velasight_provisioning_load() so a passphrase does
69:  * not travel through every callback that only wanted the notification.
70:  */
71: 
72: typedef void (*velasight_prov_saved_cb_t)(int status, uint32_t generation,
73:                                            void *arg);
74: 
75: struct velasight_prov_config_s
76: {
77:   uint16_t                  port;       /* 0 selects the built-in default */
78:   bool                      one_shot;   /* Stop after one accepted submit */
79:   const char               *store_path; /* NULL selects the built-in path */
80:   velasight_prov_saved_cb_t on_saved;   /* May be NULL */
81:   void                     *cb_arg;
82: };
83: 
84: /****************************************************************************
85:  * Name: velasight_provisioning_start
86:  *
87:  * Description:
88:  *   Bind the HTTP port and start the listener thread.  Returns 0, -EALREADY
89:  *   if it is already running, or a negative errno.  A NULL config means all
90:  *   defaults.  The config is copied, so the caller may free it.
91:  *
92:  ****************************************************************************/
93: 
94: int velasight_provisioning_start(
95:     const struct velasight_prov_config_s *config);
96: 
97: /****************************************************************************
98:  * Name: velasight_provisioning_stop
99:  *
100:  * Description:
101:  *   Close the listener and join the thread.  Returns 0, or -EALREADY when
102:  *   nothing was running.  Safe to call from the saved callback.
103:  *
104:  ****************************************************************************/
105: 
106: int velasight_provisioning_stop(void);
107: 
108: bool velasight_provisioning_is_running(void);
109: 
110: /* Saves observed in this process; 0 before the first one.  Persisted saves
111:  * from earlier boots are counted by the generation inside the record.
112:  */
113: 
114: uint32_t velasight_provisioning_generation(void);
115: 
116: /****************************************************************************
117:  * Name: velasight_provisioning_load
118:  *
119:  * Description:
120:  *   Read the stored credentials.  Returns 0, -ENOENT when nothing has been
121:  *   provisioned, -EBADMSG when the record is corrupt, or a negative errno.
122:  *
123:  ****************************************************************************/
124: 
125: int velasight_provisioning_load(
126:     struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *out);
127: 
128: int velasight_provisioning_load_from(
129:     const char *path, struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *out);
130: 
131: #ifdef __cplusplus
132: }
133: #endif
134: 
135: #endif /* __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_INCLUDE_VELASIGHT_PROVISIONING_H */

50: #include "pthread/pthread.h"
51: #include "tls/tls.h"
52: 
53: /****************************************************************************
54:  * Public Data
55:  ****************************************************************************/
56: 
57: /* Default pthread attributes (see include/nuttx/pthread.h).  When configured
58:  * to build separate kernel- and user-address spaces, this global is
59:  * duplicated in each address spaced.  This copy can only be shared within
60:  * the kernel address space.
61:  */
62: 
63: const pthread_attr_t g_default_pthread_attr = PTHREAD_ATTR_INITIALIZER;
64: 
65: /****************************************************************************
66:  * Private Functions
67:  ****************************************************************************/
68: 
69: /****************************************************************************
70:  * Name: pthread_tcb_setup
71:  *
72:  * Description:
73:  *   This function sets up parameters in the Task Control Block (TCB) in
74:  *   preparation for starting a new thread.
75:  *
76:  *   pthread_tcb_setup() is called from nxtask_init() and nxtask_start() to
77:  *   create a new task (with arguments cloned via strdup) or pthread_create()
78:  *   which has one argument passed by value (distinguished by the pthread
79:  *   boolean argument).
80:  *
81:  * Input Parameters:
82:  *   tcb        - Address of the new task's TCB
83:  *   trampoline - User space pthread startup function
84:  *   arg        - The argument to provide to the pthread on startup.
85:  *
86:  * Returned Value:
87:  *  None
88:  *
89:  ****************************************************************************/
90: 
91: static inline void pthread_tcb_setup(FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb,
92:                                      FAR struct tcb_s *parent,
93:                                      pthread_trampoline_t trampoline,
94:                                      pthread_addr_t arg)
95: {
96:   FAR struct pthread_entry_s *entry;
97: #if CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE > 0
98:   /* Copy the pthread name into the TCB */
99: 
100:   strlcpy(ptcb->name, parent->name, CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE);
101: #endif /* CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE */
102: 
103:   /* For pthreads, args are strictly pass-by-value; that actual
104:    * type wrapped by pthread_addr_t is unknown.
105:    */
106: 
107:   entry             = (FAR struct pthread_entry_s *)(ptcb + 1);
108:   entry->trampoline = trampoline;
109:   entry->arg        = arg;
110: }
111: 
112: /****************************************************************************
113:  * Name:  pthread_start
114:  *
115:  * Description:
116:  *   This function is the low level entry point into the pthread
117:  *
118:  * Input Parameters:
119:  * None
120:  *
121:  ****************************************************************************/
122: 
123: static void pthread_start(void)
124: {
125:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb = this_task();
126:   FAR struct pthread_entry_s *entry =
127:     (FAR struct pthread_entry_s *)(ptcb + 1);
128:   pthread_startroutine_t pthread = ptcb->entry.pthread;
129:   pthread_trampoline_t trampoline = entry->trampoline;
130:   pthread_addr_t arg = entry->arg;
131: 
132:   /* The priority of this thread may have been boosted to avoid priority
133:    * inversion problems.  If that is the case, then drop to the correct
134:    * execution priority.
135:    */
136: 
137:   if (ptcb->sched_priority > ptcb->init_priority)
138:     {
139:       DEBUGVERIFY(nxsched_set_priority(ptcb, ptcb->init_priority));
140:     }
141: 
142:   /* Pass control to the thread entry point. In the kernel build this has to
143:    * be handled differently if we are starting a user-space pthread; we have
144:    * to switch to user-mode before calling into the pthread.
145:    */
146: 
147:   DEBUGASSERT(trampoline != NULL && pthread != NULL);
148: 
149: #ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
150:   up_addrenv_leave_kernel();
151:   trampoline(pthread, arg);
152: #else
153:   up_pthread_start(trampoline, pthread, arg);
154: #endif
155: 
156:   /* The thread has returned (should never happen) */
157: 
158:   DEBUGPANIC();
159:   pthread_exit(NULL);
160: }
161: 
162: /****************************************************************************
163:  * Public Functions
164:  ****************************************************************************/
165: 
166: /****************************************************************************
167:  * Name:  nx_pthread_create
168:  *
169:  * Description:
170:  *   This function creates and activates a new thread with specified
171:  *   attributes.
172:  *
173:  * Input Parameters:
174:  *    trampoline - The user space startup function
175:  *    thread     - The pthread handle to be used
176:  *    attr       - It points to a pthread_attr_t structure whose contents are
177:  *                 used at thread creation time to determine attributes
178:  *                 for the new thread
179:  *    entry      - The new thread starts execution by invoking entry
180:  *    arg        - It is passed as the sole argument of entry
181:  *
182:  * Returned Value:
183:  *   OK (0) on success; a (non-negated) errno value on failure. The errno
184:  *   variable is not set.
185:  *
186:  ****************************************************************************/
187: 
188: int nx_pthread_create(pthread_trampoline_t trampoline, FAR pthread_t *thread,
189:                       FAR const pthread_attr_t *attr,
190:                       pthread_startroutine_t entry, pthread_addr_t arg)
191: {
192:   pthread_attr_t default_attr;
193:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;
194:   struct sched_param param;
195:   FAR struct tcb_s *parent;
196:   int policy;
197:   int errcode;
198:   int ret;
199: 
200:   DEBUGASSERT(trampoline != NULL);
201: 
202:   parent = this_task();
203:   DEBUGASSERT(parent != NULL);
204: 
205:   /* If attributes were not supplied, use the default attributes */
206: 
207:   if (!attr)
208:     {
209:       pthread_attr_init(&default_attr);
210:       attr = &default_attr;
211:     }
212:   else if (attr->priority < SCHED_PRIORITY_MIN ||
213:            attr->priority > SCHED_PRIORITY_MAX)
214:     {
215:       return EINVAL;
216:     }
217: 
218:   /* Allocate a TCB for the new task. */
219: 
220:   ptcb = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct tcb_s) + sizeof(struct pthread_entry_s));
221:   if (!ptcb)
222:     {
223:       serr("ERROR: Failed to allocate TCB\n");
224:       return ENOMEM;
225:     }
226: 
227:   atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_FREE_TCB);
228: 
229:   /* Initialize the task join */
230: 
231:   nxtask_joininit(ptcb);
232: 
233:   nxsem_init(&ptcb->exit_sem, 0, 0);
234: 
235:   /* Bind the parent's group to the new TCB (we have not yet joined the
236:    * group).
237:    */
238: 
239:   group_bind(ptcb);
240: 
241: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
242:   /* Share the address environment of the parent task group. */
243: 
244:   ret = addrenv_join(this_task(), ptcb);
245:   if (ret < 0)
246:     {
247:       errcode = -ret;
248:       goto errout_with_tcb;
249:     }
250: #endif
251: 
252:   if (attr->detachstate == PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED)
253:     {
254:       atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_DETACHED);
255:     }
256: 
257:   if (attr->stackaddr)
258:     {
259:       /* Use pre-allocated stack */
260: 
261:       ret = up_use_stack(ptcb, attr->stackaddr, attr->stacksize,
262:                          TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
263:     }
264:   else
265:     {
266:       /* Allocate the stack for the TCB */
267: 
268:       ret = up_create_stack(ptcb, attr->stacksize + attr->guardsize,
269:                             TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
270:     }
271: 
272:   if (ret != OK)
273:     {
274:       errcode = ENOMEM;
275:       goto errout_with_tcb;
276:     }
277: 
278: #if defined(CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACK)
279:   /* Allocate the kernel stack */
280: 
281:   ret = up_addrenv_kstackalloc(ptcb);
282:   if (ret < 0)
283:     {
284:       errcode = ENOMEM;
285:       goto errout_with_tcb;
286:     }
287: #endif
288: 
289:   /* Should we use the priority and scheduler specified in the pthread
290:    * attributes?  Or should we use the current thread's priority and
291:    * scheduler?
292:    */
293: 
294:   if (attr->inheritsched == PTHREAD_INHERIT_SCHED)
295:     {
296:       /* Get the priority (and any other scheduling parameters) for this
297:        * thread.
298:        */
299: 
300:       ret = nxsched_get_param(0, &param);
301:       if (ret < 0)
302:         {
303:           errcode = -ret;
304:           goto errout_with_tcb;
305:         }
306: 
307:       /* Get the scheduler policy for this thread */
308: 
309:       policy = nxsched_get_scheduler(0);
310:       if (policy < 0)
311:         {
312:           errcode = -policy;
313:           goto errout_with_tcb;
314:         }
315:     }
316:   else
317:     {
318:       /* Use the scheduler policy and policy the attributes */
319: 
320:       policy                             = attr->policy;
321:       param.sched_priority               = attr->priority;
322: 
323: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
324:       param.sched_ss_low_priority        = attr->low_priority;
325:       param.sched_ss_max_repl            = attr->max_repl;
326:       param.sched_ss_repl_period.tv_sec  = attr->repl_period.tv_sec;
327:       param.sched_ss_repl_period.tv_nsec = attr->repl_period.tv_nsec;
328:       param.sched_ss_init_budget.tv_sec  = attr->budget.tv_sec;
329:       param.sched_ss_init_budget.tv_nsec = attr->budget.tv_nsec;
330: #endif
331:     }
332: 
333: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
334:   if (policy == SCHED_SPORADIC)
335:     {
336:       FAR struct sporadic_s *sporadic;
337:       sclock_t repl_ticks;
338:       sclock_t budget_ticks;
339: 
340:       /* Convert timespec values to system clock ticks */
341: 
342:       repl_ticks = clock_time2ticks(&param.sched_ss_repl_period);
343:       budget_ticks = clock_time2ticks(&param.sched_ss_init_budget);
344: 
345:       /* The replenishment period must be greater than or equal to the
346:        * budget period.
347:        */
348: 
349:       if (repl_ticks < budget_ticks)
350:         {
351:           errcode = EINVAL;
352:           goto errout_with_tcb;
353:         }
354: 
355:       /* Initialize the sporadic policy */
356: 
357:       ret = nxsched_initialize_sporadic(ptcb);
358:       if (ret >= 0)
359:         {
360:           sporadic               = ptcb->sporadic;
361:           DEBUGASSERT(sporadic != NULL);
362: 
363:           /* Save the sporadic scheduling parameters */
364: 
365:           sporadic->hi_priority  = param.sched_priority;
366:           sporadic->low_priority = param.sched_ss_low_priority;
367:           sporadic->max_repl     = param.sched_ss_max_repl;
368:           sporadic->repl_period  = repl_ticks;
369:           sporadic->budget       = budget_ticks;
370: 
371:           /* And start the first replenishment interval */
372: 
373:           ret = nxsched_start_sporadic(ptcb);
374:         }
375: 
376:       /* Handle any failures */
377: 
378:       if (ret < 0)
379:         {
380:           errcode = -ret;
381:           goto errout_with_tcb;
382:         }
383:     }
384: #endif
385: 
386:   /* Initialize thread local storage */
387: 
388:   ret = tls_init_info(ptcb);
389:   if (ret != OK)
390:     {
391:       errcode = -ret;
392:       goto errout_with_tcb;
393:     }
394: 
395:   /* Configure the TCB for a pthread receiving on parameter
396:    * passed by value
397:    */
398: 
399:   pthread_tcb_setup(ptcb, parent, trampoline, arg);
400: 
401:   /* Initialize the task control block */
402: 
403:   ret = pthread_setup_scheduler(ptcb, param.sched_priority, pthread_start,
404:                                 entry);
405:   if (ret != OK)
406:     {
407:       errcode = EBUSY;
408:       goto errout_with_tcb;
409:     }
410: 
411: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
412:   /* pthread_setup_scheduler() will set the affinity mask by inheriting the
413:    * setting from the parent task.  We need to override this setting
414:    * with the value from the pthread attributes unless that value is
415:    * zero:  Zero is the default value and simply means to inherit the
416:    * parent thread's affinity mask.
417:    */
418: 
419:   if (attr->affinity != 0)
420:     {
421:       ptcb->affinity = attr->affinity;
422:     }
423: #endif
424: 
425:   /* Join the parent's task group */
426: 
427:   group_join(ptcb);
428: 
429:   /* Set the appropriate scheduling policy in the TCB */
430: 
431:   atomic_and(&ptcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK);
432: 
433:   switch (policy)
434:     {
435:       default:
436:       case SCHED_FIFO:
437:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_FIFO);
438:         break;
439: 
440: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
441:       case SCHED_OTHER:
442:       case SCHED_RR:
443:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
444:         ptcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
445:         break;
446: #endif
447: 
448: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
449:       case SCHED_SPORADIC:
450:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC);
451:         break;
452: #endif
453:     }
454: 
455:   /* Return the thread information to the caller */
456: 
457:   if (thread != NULL)
458:     {
459:       *thread = (pthread_t)ptcb->pid;
460:     }
461: 
462:   /* Then activate the task */
463: 
464:   nxtask_activate(ptcb);
465: 
466:   return OK;
467: 
468: errout_with_tcb:
469: 
470:   /* Since we do not join the group, assign group to NULL to clear binding */
471: 
472:   ptcb->group = NULL;
473: 
474:   nxsched_release_tcb(ptcb, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
475:   return errcode;
476: }

55:                             pthread_addr_t arg)

60:

398:   else
399:     {

401:       return true;
402:     }

408: /****************************************************************************
409:  * Name: dhcpd_setlease
410:  ****************************************************************************/

412: struct lease_s *dhcpd_setlease(const uint8_t *mac,
413:                                in_addr_t ipaddr, time_t expiry)
414: {
415:   /* Calculate the offset from the first IP address managed by DHCPD.
416:    * ipaddr must be in host order!
417:    */
418: 
419:   int ndx = ipaddr - g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip;
420:   struct lease_s *ret = NULL;
421: 
422:   ninfo("ipaddr: %08" PRIx32 " ipaddr: %08" PRIx32 " ndx: %d MAX: %d\n",
423:         (uint32_t)ipaddr, (uint32_t)g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip, ndx,
424:         CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MAXLEASES);
425: 
426:   /* Verify that the address offset is within the supported range */
427: 
428:   if (ndx >= 0 && ndx < CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MAXLEASES)
429:     {
430:        ret = &g_state.ds_leases[ndx];
431:        memcpy(ret->mac, mac, DHCP_HLEN_ETHERNET);
432:        ret->allocated = true;
433: #ifdef HAVE_LEASE_TIME
434:        ret->expiry = dhcpd_time() + expiry;
435: #endif
436:     }
437: 
438:   return ret;
439: }

441: /****************************************************************************
442:  * Name: dhcp_leaseipaddr
443:  ****************************************************************************/
444: 
445: static inline in_addr_t dhcp_leaseipaddr(FAR struct lease_s *lease)
446: {
447:   /* Return IP address in host order */
448: 
449:   return (in_addr_t)(lease - g_state.ds_leases) +
450:          g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip;
451: }

453: /****************************************************************************
454:  * Name: dhcpd_findbymac
455:  ****************************************************************************/
456: 
457: static FAR struct lease_s *dhcpd_findbymac(FAR const uint8_t *mac)
458: {
459:   int i;
460: 
461:   for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MAXLEASES; i++)
462:     {
463:       if (memcmp(g_state.ds_leases[i].mac, mac, DHCP_HLEN_ETHERNET) == 0)
464:         {
465:           return &(g_state.ds_leases[i]);
466:         }
467:     }
468: 
469:   return NULL;
470: }
471: 
472: /****************************************************************************
473:  * Name: dhcpd_findbyipaddr
474:  ****************************************************************************/
475: 
476: static FAR struct lease_s *dhcpd_findbyipaddr(in_addr_t ipaddr)
477: {
478:   if (ipaddr >= g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip &&
479:       ipaddr <= g_dhcpd_config.ds_endip)
480:     {
481:       FAR struct lease_s *lease =
482:         &g_state.ds_leases[ipaddr - g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip];
483:       if (lease->allocated > 0)
484:         {
485:           return lease;
486:         }
487:     }
488: 
489:   return NULL;
490: }
491: 
492: /****************************************************************************
493:  * Name: dhcpd_allocipaddr
494:  ****************************************************************************/
495: 
496: static in_addr_t dhcpd_allocipaddr(void)
497: {
498:   struct lease_s *lease = NULL;
499:   in_addr_t ipaddr, startaddr;
500: 
501:   ipaddr = startaddr = g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip;
502:   for (; ipaddr <= g_dhcpd_config.ds_endip; ipaddr++)
503:     {
504:       /* Skip over address ending in 0 or 255 */
505: 
506:       if ((ipaddr & 0xff) == 0 || (ipaddr & 0xff) == 0xff)
507:         {
508:           continue;
509:         }
510: 
511:       /* Is there already a lease on this address?  If so, has it expired? */
512: 
513:       lease = dhcpd_findbyipaddr(ipaddr);
514:       if ((!lease || dhcpd_leaseexpired(lease)))
515:         {
516: #ifdef CONFIG_CPP_HAVE_WARNING
517: #  warning "FIXME: Should check if anything responds to an ARP request or ping"
518: #  warning "       to verify that there is no other user of this IP address"
519: #endif
520:           memset(g_state.ds_leases[ipaddr - startaddr].mac,
521:           0, DHCP_HLEN_ETHERNET);
522:           g_state.ds_leases[ipaddr - startaddr].allocated = true;
523: #ifdef HAVE_LEASE_TIME
524:           g_state.ds_leases[ipaddr - startaddr].expiry =
525:             dhcpd_time() + CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_OFFERTIME;
526: #endif
527:           /* Return the address in host order */
528: 
529:           return ipaddr;
530:         }
531:     }
532: 
533:   return 0;
534: }

539: 
540: static inline bool dhcpd_parseoptions(void)
541: {
542:   uint32_t tmp;
543:   uint8_t *ptr;
544: #ifndef CONFIG_NET_DHCP_LIGHT
545:   uint8_t overloaded;
546:   uint8_t currfield;
547: #endif
548:   int optlen = 0;
549:   int remaining;
550: 
551:   /* Verify that the option field starts with a valid magic number */
552: 
553:   ptr = g_state.ds_inpacket.options;
554:   if (memcmp(ptr, g_magiccookie, 4) != 0)
555:     {
556:       /* Bad magic number... skip g_state.ds_outpacket */
557: 
558:       nerr("ERROR: Bad magic: %d,%d,%d,%d\n",
559:            ptr[0], ptr[1], ptr[2], ptr[3]);
560:       return false;
561:     }
562: 
563:   /* Set up to parse the options */
564: 
565:   ptr       += 4;
566:   remaining  = DHCPD_OPTIONS_SIZE - 4;
567: #ifndef CONFIG_NET_DHCP_LIGHT
568:   overloaded = DHCPD_OPTION_FIELD;
569:   currfield  = DHCPD_OPTION_FIELD;
570: #endif
571: 
572:   /* Set all options to the default value */
573: 
574:   g_state.ds_optmsgtype   = 0;    /* Incoming DHCP message type */
575:   g_state.ds_optreqip     = 0;    /* Requested IP address (host order) */
576:   g_state.ds_optserverip  = 0;    /* Serverip IP address (host order) */
577:   g_state.ds_optleasetime = 0;    /* Requested lease time (host order) */
578:   g_state.ds_optend       = NULL;
579: 
580:   do
581:     {
582:       /* The form of an option is:
583:        *   code   - 1 byte
584:        *   length - 1 byte
585:        *   data   - variable number of bytes
586:        */
587: 
588:       switch (ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_CODE])
589:         {
590:           /* Skip over any padding bytes */
591: 
592:           case DHCP_OPTION_PAD:
593:             optlen = 1;
594:             break;
595: 
596:           /* the Overload option is used to indicate that the DHCP 'sname'
597:            * or 'file' fields are being overloaded by using them to carry
598:            * DHCP options. A DHCP server inserts this option if the
599:            * returned parameters will exceed the usual space allotted for
600:            * options.
601:            *
602:            * If this option is present, the client interprets the specified
603:            * additional fields after it concludes interpretation of the
604:            * standard option fields.
605:            *
606:            * Legal values for this option are:
607:            *
608:            *   1     the 'file' field is used to hold options
609:            *   2     the 'sname' field is used to hold options
610:            *   3     both fields are used to hold options
611:            */
612: 
613: #ifndef CONFIG_NET_DHCP_LIGHT
614:           case DHCP_OPTION_OVERLOAD:
615:             optlen = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
616:             if (optlen >= 3 && optlen < remaining)
617:               {
618:                 overloaded = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_DATA];
619:               }
620:             break;
621: #endif
622: 
623:           case DHCP_OPTION_END:
624: #ifndef CONFIG_NET_DHCP_LIGHT
625:             if (currfield == DHCPD_OPTION_FIELD &&
626:                 (overloaded & DHCPD_FILE_FIELD) != 0)
627:               {
628:                 ptr       = g_state.ds_inpacket.file;
629:                 remaining = sizeof(g_state.ds_inpacket.file);
630:                 currfield = DHCPD_FILE_FIELD;
631:               }
632:             else if (currfield == DHCPD_FILE_FIELD &&
633:                      (overloaded & DHCPD_SNAME_FIELD) != 0)
634:               {
635:                 ptr       = g_state.ds_inpacket.sname;
636:                 remaining = sizeof(g_state.ds_inpacket.sname);
637:                 currfield = DHCPD_SNAME_FIELD;
638:               }
639:             else
640:               {
641:                 return true;
642:               }
643:             break;
644: #else
645:             return true;
646: #endif
647: 
648:           case DHCP_OPTION_REQ_IPADDR: /* Requested IP Address */
649:             optlen = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
650:             if (optlen >= 6 && optlen < remaining)
651:               {
652:                 memcpy(&tmp, &ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_DATA], 4);
653:                 g_state.ds_optreqip = (in_addr_t)ntohl(tmp);
654:               }
655:             break;
656: 
657:           case DHCP_OPTION_LEASE_TIME: /* IP address lease time */
658:              optlen = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
659:             if (optlen >= 6 && optlen < remaining)
660:               {
661:                 memcpy(&tmp, &ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_DATA], 4);
662:                 g_state.ds_optleasetime = (time_t)ntohl(tmp);
663:               }
664:             break;
665: 
666:          case DHCP_OPTION_MSG_TYPE: /* DHCP message type */
667:             optlen = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
668:             if (optlen >= 3 && optlen < remaining)
669:               {
670:                 g_state.ds_optmsgtype = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_DATA];
671:               }
672:             break;
673: 
674:           case DHCP_OPTION_SERVER_ID: /* Server identifier */
675:             optlen = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
676:             if (optlen >= 6 && optlen < remaining)
677:               {
678:                 memcpy(&tmp, &ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_DATA], 4);
679:                 g_state.ds_optserverip = (in_addr_t)ntohl(tmp);
680:               }
681:             break;
682: 
683:           default:
684: 
685:             /* Skip over unsupported options */
686: 
687:             optlen = ptr[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
688:             break;
689:         }
690: 
691:       /* Advance to the next option */
692: 
693:       ptr       += optlen;
694:       remaining -= optlen;
695:     }
696:   while (remaining > 0);
697: 
698:   return false;
699: }

701: /****************************************************************************
702:  * Name: dhcpd_verifyreqip
703:  ****************************************************************************/
704: 
705: static inline bool dhcpd_verifyreqip(void)
706: {
707:   struct lease_s *lease;
708: 
709:   /* Verify that the requested IP address is within the supported lease
710:    * range
711:    */
712: 
713:   if (g_state.ds_optreqip >= g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip &&
714:       g_state.ds_optreqip <= g_dhcpd_config.ds_endip)
715:     {
716:       /* And verify that the lease has not already been taken or offered
717:        * (unless the lease/offer is expired, then the address is free game).
718:        */
719: 
720:       lease = dhcpd_findbyipaddr(g_state.ds_optreqip);
721:       if (!lease || dhcpd_leaseexpired(lease))
722:         {
723:           return true;
724:         }
725:     }
726: 
727:   return false;
728: }

730: /****************************************************************************
731:  * Name: dhcpd_verifyreqleasetime
732:  ****************************************************************************/
733: 
734: static inline bool dhcpd_verifyreqleasetime(uint32_t *leasetime)
735: {
736:   uint32_t tmp = g_state.ds_optleasetime;
737: 
738:   /* Did the client request a specific lease time? */
739: 
740:   if (tmp != 0)
741:     {
742:       /* Yes..  Verify that the requested lease time is within a
743:        * valid range
744:        */
745: 
746:       if (tmp > CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MAXLEASETIME)
747:         {
748:           tmp = CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MAXLEASETIME;
749:         }
750:       else if (tmp < CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MINLEASETIME)
751:         {
752:           tmp = CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MINLEASETIME;
753:         }
754: 
755:       /* Return the clipped lease time */
756: 
757:       *leasetime = tmp;
758:       return true;
759:     }
760: 
761:   return false;
762: }

766:  ****************************************************************************/

768: static int dhcpd_addoption(uint8_t *option)
769: {
770:   int offset;
771:   int len = 4;
772: 
773:   if (g_state.ds_optend)
774:     {
775:       offset = g_state.ds_optend - g_state.ds_outpacket.options;
776:       len    = option[DHCPD_OPTION_LENGTH] + 2;
777: 
778:       /* Check if the option will fit into the options array */
779: 
780:       if (offset + len + 1 < DHCPD_OPTIONS_SIZE)
781:         {
782:           /* Copy the option into the option array */
783: 
784:           memcpy(g_state.ds_optend, option, len);
785:           g_state.ds_optend += len;
786:          *g_state.ds_optend  = DHCP_OPTION_END;
787:         }
788:     }
789: 
790:   return len;
791: }

852: /****************************************************************************
853:  * Name: dhcpd_socket
854:  ****************************************************************************/
855: 
856: static inline int dhcpd_socket(FAR const char *interface)
857: {
858:   int sockfd;
859: #if defined(HAVE_SO_REUSEADDR) || defined(HAVE_SO_BROADCAST)
860:   int optval;
861:   int ret;
862: #endif
863: 
864:   /* Create a socket to listen for requests from DHCP clients */
865: 
866:   sockfd = socket(PF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
867:   if (sockfd < 0)
868:     {
869:       nerr("ERROR: socket failed: %d\n", errno);
870:       return ERROR;
871:     }
872: 
873:   /* Configure the socket */
874: 
875: #ifdef HAVE_SO_REUSEADDR
876:   optval = 1;
877:   ret = setsockopt(sockfd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, (FAR void *)&optval,
878:                    sizeof(int));
879:   if (ret < 0)
880:     {
881:       nerr("ERROR: setsockopt SO_REUSEADDR failed: %d\n", errno);
882:       close(sockfd);
883:       return ERROR;
884:     }
885: #endif
886: 
887: #ifdef HAVE_SO_BROADCAST
888:   optval = 1;
889:   ret = setsockopt(sockfd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST, (FAR void *)&optval,
890:                    sizeof(int));
891:   if (ret < 0)
892:     {
893:       nerr("ERROR: setsockopt SO_BROADCAST failed: %d\n", errno);
894:       close(sockfd);
895:       return ERROR;
896:     }
897: #endif
898: 
899: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_BINDTODEVICE
900:   /* Bind socket to interface, because UDP packets have to be sent to the
901:    * broadcast address at a moment when it is not possible to decide the
902:    * target network device using the local or remote address (which is,
903:    * by definition and purpose of DHCP, undefined yet).
904:    */
905: 
906:   if (setsockopt(sockfd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BINDTODEVICE,
907:                  interface, strlen(interface)) < 0)
908:     {
909:       ninfo("ERROR: setsockopt SO_BINDTODEVICE failed: %d\n", errno);
910:       close(sockfd);
911:       return ERROR;
912:     }
913: #endif
914: 
915:   return sockfd;
916: }

918: /****************************************************************************
919:  * Name: dhcpd_initpacket
920:  ****************************************************************************/
921: 
922: static void dhcpd_initpacket(uint8_t mtype)
923: {
924:   uint32_t nulladdr = 0;
925: 
926:   /* Set up the generic parts of the DHCP server message */
927: 
928:   memset(&g_state.ds_outpacket, 0, sizeof(struct dhcpmsg_s));
929: 
930:   g_state.ds_outpacket.op         = DHCP_REPLY;
931:   g_state.ds_outpacket.htype      = g_state.ds_inpacket.htype;
932:   g_state.ds_outpacket.hlen       = g_state.ds_inpacket.hlen;
933: 
934:   memcpy(&g_state.ds_outpacket.xid, &g_state.ds_inpacket.xid, 4);
935:   memcpy(g_state.ds_outpacket.chaddr, g_state.ds_inpacket.chaddr, 16);
936: 
937:   if (memcmp(g_state.ds_outpacket.giaddr, &nulladdr, 4) != 0)
938:     {
939:       g_state.ds_outpacket.flags  = g_state.ds_inpacket.flags;
940:     }
941: 
942:   /* Add the generic options */
943: 
944:   memcpy(g_state.ds_outpacket.options, g_magiccookie, 4);
945:   g_state.ds_optend = &g_state.ds_outpacket.options[4];
946:  *g_state.ds_optend = DHCP_OPTION_END;
947:   dhcpd_addoption8(DHCP_OPTION_MSG_TYPE, mtype);
948:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_SERVER_ID, g_state.ds_serverip);
949: }
