951: /****************************************************************************
952:  * Name: dhcpd_sendpacket
953:  ****************************************************************************/
954: 
955: static int dhcpd_sendpacket(int sockfd, int bbroadcast)
956: {
957:   struct sockaddr_in addr;
958:   in_addr_t ipaddr;
959:   int len;
960: 
961: #ifdef CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_IGNOREBROADCAST
962:   /* This is a hack.  I've had problems with Windows machines responding
963:    * to unicast.  I think this is associated with a Windows registry key in
964:    * HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\
965:    * SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DHCPServer\Parameters:
966:    * The IgnoreBroadcastFlag value controls this behavior:  A value of 1 will
967:    * cause the server to ignore the client broadcast flag and always respond
968:    * with multicast; the value 0 to allows clients to request unicast.
969:    */
970: 
971:   ipaddr = INADDR_BROADCAST;
972: #else
973:   const uint8_t anyipaddr[4] =
974:   {
975:   };
976: 
977:   /* Determine which address to respond to (or if we need to broadcast the
978:    * response)
979:    *
980:    * (1) If he caller know that it needs to multicast the response, it will
981:    *     set broadcast.
982:    * (2) Otherwise, if the client already has and address (ciaddr), then use
983:    *     that for unicast
984:    * (3) Broadcast if the client says it can't handle uni-cast
985:    *     (BOOTP_BROADCAST set)
986:    * (4) Otherwise, the client claims it can handle the uni-casst response
987:    *     and we will uni-cast to the offered address (yiaddr).
988:    *
989:    * NOTE: We really should also check the giaddr field.  If no zero, the
990:    * server should send any return messages to the 'DHCP server' port on the
991:    *  BOOTP relay agent whose address appears in 'giaddr'.
992:    */
993: 
994:   if (bbroadcast)
995:     {
996:       ipaddr = INADDR_BROADCAST;
997:     }
998:   else if (memcmp(g_state.ds_outpacket.ciaddr, anyipaddr, 4) != 0)
999:     {
1000:       dhcpd_arpupdate(g_state.ds_outpacket.ciaddr,
1001:                       g_state.ds_outpacket.chaddr);
1002:       memcpy(&ipaddr, g_state.ds_outpacket.ciaddr, 4);
1003:     }
1004:   else if (g_state.ds_outpacket.flags & HTONS(BOOTP_BROADCAST))
1005:     {
1006:       ipaddr = INADDR_BROADCAST;
1007:     }
1008:   else
1009:     {
1010:       dhcpd_arpupdate(g_state.ds_outpacket.yiaddr,
1011:                       g_state.ds_outpacket.chaddr);
1012:       memcpy(&ipaddr, g_state.ds_outpacket.yiaddr, 4);
1013:     }
1014: #endif
1015: 
1016:   /* Create a socket to respond with a packet to the client.  We
1017:    * cannot re-use the listener socket because it is not bound correctly
1018:    */
1019: 
1020:   /* Then send the response to the DHCP client port at that address */
1021: 
1022:   memset(&addr, 0, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in));
1023:   addr.sin_family      = AF_INET;
1024:   addr.sin_port        = HTONS(DHCP_CLIENT_PORT);
1025:   addr.sin_addr.s_addr = ipaddr;
1026: 
1027:   /* Send the minimum sized packet that includes the END option */
1028: 
1029:   len = (g_state.ds_optend - (FAR uint8_t *)&g_state.ds_outpacket) + 1;
1030:   ninfo("sendto %08lx:%04x len=%d\n",
1031:         (long)ntohl(addr.sin_addr.s_addr), ntohs(addr.sin_port), len);
1032: 
1033:   return sendto(sockfd, &g_state.ds_outpacket, len, 0,
1034:                 (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in));
1035: }
1036: 
1037: /****************************************************************************
1038:  * Name: dhcpd_sendoffer
1039:  ****************************************************************************/
1040: 
1041: static inline int dhcpd_sendoffer(int sockfd, in_addr_t ipaddr,
1042:                                   uint32_t leasetime)
1043: {
1044:   in_addr_t netaddr;
1045: #ifdef HAVE_DNSIP
1046:   uint32_t dnsaddr;
1047:   dnsaddr = htonl(g_dhcpd_config.ds_dnsip);
1048: #endif
1049:   /* IP address is in host order */
1050: 
1051:   ninfo("Sending offer: %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1052: 
1053:   /* Initialize the outgoing packet */
1054: 
1055:   dhcpd_initpacket(DHCPOFFER);
1056: 
1057:   /* Add the address offered to the client (converting to network order) */
1058: 
1059:   netaddr = htonl(ipaddr);
1060:   memcpy(g_state.ds_outpacket.yiaddr, &netaddr, 4);
1061: 
1062:   /* Add the leasetime to the response options */
1063: 
1064:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_LEASE_TIME, htonl(leasetime));
1065: #ifdef HAVE_NETMASK
1066:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_SUBNET_MASK,
1067:                     htonl(g_dhcpd_config.ds_netmask));
1068: #endif
1069: #ifdef HAVE_ROUTERIP
1070:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_ROUTER,
1071:                     htonl(g_dhcpd_config.ds_routerip));
1072: #endif
1073: #ifdef HAVE_DNSIP
1074:   dhcp_addoption32p(DHCP_OPTION_DNS_SERVER, (FAR uint8_t *)&dnsaddr);
1075: #endif
1076: 
1077:   /* Send the offer response */
1078: 
1079: #ifdef CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_IGNOREBROADCAST
1080:   return dhcpd_sendpacket(sockfd, true);
1081: #else
1082:   return dhcpd_sendpacket(sockfd, false);
1083: #endif
1084: }

1087:  * Name: dhcpd_sendnak

1089: 
1090: static int dhcpd_sendnak(int sockfd)
1091: {

1093: 
1094:   dhcpd_initpacket(DHCPNAK);
1095:   memcpy(g_state.ds_outpacket.ciaddr, g_state.ds_inpacket.ciaddr, 4);
1096:   return dhcpd_sendpacket(sockfd, true);

1099: /****************************************************************************
1100:  * Name: dhcpd_sendack
1101:  ****************************************************************************/
1102: 
1103: int dhcpd_sendack(int sockfd, in_addr_t ipaddr)
1104: {
1105:   uint32_t leasetime = CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_LEASETIME;
1106:   in_addr_t netaddr;
1107: #ifdef HAVE_DNSIP
1108:   uint32_t dnsaddr;
1109:   dnsaddr = htonl(g_dhcpd_config.ds_dnsip);
1110: #endif
1111: 
1112:   /* Initialize the ACK response */
1113: 
1114:   dhcpd_initpacket(DHCPACK);
1115:   memcpy(g_state.ds_outpacket.ciaddr, g_state.ds_inpacket.ciaddr, 4);
1116: 
1117:   /* Add the IP address assigned to the client */
1118: 
1119:   netaddr = htonl(ipaddr);
1120:   memcpy(g_state.ds_outpacket.yiaddr, &netaddr, 4);
1121: 
1122:   /* Did the client request a specific lease time? */
1123: 
1124:   dhcpd_verifyreqleasetime(&leasetime);
1125: 
1126:   /* Add the lease time to the response */
1127: 
1128:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_LEASE_TIME, htonl(leasetime));
1129: #ifdef HAVE_NETMASK
1130:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_SUBNET_MASK,
1131:                     htonl(g_dhcpd_config.ds_netmask));
1132: #endif
1133: #ifdef HAVE_ROUTERIP
1134:   dhcpd_addoption32(DHCP_OPTION_ROUTER,
1135:                     htonl(g_dhcpd_config.ds_routerip));
1136: #endif
1137: #ifdef HAVE_DNSIP
1138:   dhcp_addoption32p(DHCP_OPTION_DNS_SERVER, (FAR uint8_t *)&dnsaddr);
1139: #endif
1140: 
1141: #ifdef CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_IGNOREBROADCAST
1142:   if (dhcpd_sendpacket(sockfd, true) < 0)
1143: #else
1144:   if (dhcpd_sendpacket(sockfd, false) < 0)
1145: #endif
1146:     {
1147:       return ERROR;
1148:     }
1149: 
1150:   dhcpd_setlease(g_state.ds_inpacket.chaddr, ipaddr, leasetime);
1151:   return OK;
1152: }

1154: /****************************************************************************
1155:  * Name: dhcpd_discover
1156:  ****************************************************************************/
1157: 
1158: static inline int dhcpd_discover(int sockfd)
1159: {
1160:   struct lease_s *lease;
1161:   in_addr_t ipaddr;
1162:   uint32_t leasetime = CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_LEASETIME;
1163: 
1164:   /* Check if the client is already in the lease table */
1165: 
1166:   lease = dhcpd_findbymac(g_state.ds_inpacket.chaddr);
1167:   if (lease)
1168:     {
1169:       /* Yes... get the remaining time on the lease */
1170: 
1171: #ifdef HAVE_LEASE_TIME
1172:       if (!dhcpd_leaseexpired(lease))
1173:         {
1174:           leasetime = lease->expiry - dhcpd_time();
1175:           if (leasetime < CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MINLEASETIME)
1176:             {
1177:               leasetime = CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_MINLEASETIME;
1178:             }
1179:         }
1180: #endif
1181: 
1182:       /* Get the IP address associated with the lease (host order) */
1183: 
1184:       ipaddr = dhcp_leaseipaddr(lease);
1185:       ninfo("Already have lease for IP %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1186:     }
1187: 
1188:   /* Check if the client has requested a specific IP address */
1189: 
1190:   else if (dhcpd_verifyreqip())
1191:     {
1192:       /* Use the requested IP address (host order) */
1193: 
1194:       ipaddr = g_state.ds_optreqip;
1195:       ninfo("User requested IP %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1196:     }
1197:   else
1198:     {
1199:       /* No... allocate a new IP address (host order) */
1200: 
1201:       ipaddr = dhcpd_allocipaddr();
1202:       ninfo("Allocated IP %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1203:     }
1204: 
1205:   /* Did we get any IP address? */
1206: 
1207:   if (!ipaddr)
1208:     {
1209:       /* Nope... return failure */
1210: 
1211:       nerr("ERROR: Failed to get IP address\n");
1212:       return ERROR;
1213:     }
1214: 
1215:   /* Reserve the leased IP for a shorter time for the offer */
1216: 
1217:   if (!dhcpd_setlease(g_state.ds_inpacket.chaddr, ipaddr,
1218:                       CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_OFFERTIME))
1219:     {
1220:       nerr("ERROR: Failed to set lease\n");
1221:       return ERROR;
1222:     }
1223: 
1224:   /* Check if the client has requested a specific lease time */
1225: 
1226:   dhcpd_verifyreqleasetime(&leasetime);
1227: 
1228:   /* Send the offer response */
1229: 
1230:   return dhcpd_sendoffer(sockfd, ipaddr, leasetime);
1231: }

1233: /****************************************************************************
1234:  * Name: dhcpd_request
1235:  ****************************************************************************/
1236: 
1237: static inline int dhcpd_request(int sockfd)
1238: {
1239:   struct lease_s *lease;
1240:   in_addr_t ipaddr = 0;
1241:   uint8_t response = 0;
1242: 
1243:   /* Check if this client already holds a lease. This can happen when the
1244:    * client (1) the IP is reserved for the client from a previous offer,
1245:    * or (2) the client is re-initializing or rebooting while the lease is
1246:    * still valid.
1247:    */
1248: 
1249:   lease = dhcpd_findbymac(g_state.ds_inpacket.chaddr);
1250:   if (lease)
1251:     {
1252:       /* Yes.. the client already holds a lease.  Verify that the request is
1253:        * consistent* with the existing lease (host order).
1254:        */
1255: 
1256:       ipaddr = dhcp_leaseipaddr(lease);
1257:       ninfo("Lease ipaddr: %08" PRIx32 " Server IP: %08" PRIx32
1258:             " Requested IP: %08" PRIx32 "\n",
1259:             (uint32_t)ipaddr,
1260:             (uint32_t)g_state.ds_optserverip,
1261:             (uint32_t)g_state.ds_optreqip);
1262: 
1263:       if (g_state.ds_optserverip)
1264:         {
1265:           /* ACK if the serverip is correct and the requested IP address is
1266:            * the one already offered to the client.
1267:            */
1268: 
1269:           if (g_state.ds_optserverip == ntohl(g_state.ds_serverip) &&
1270:              (g_state.ds_optreqip != 0 || g_state.ds_optreqip == ipaddr))
1271:             {
1272:               response = DHCPACK;
1273:             }
1274:           else
1275:             {
1276:               response = DHCPNAK;
1277:             }
1278:         }
1279: 
1280:       /* We have the lease and no server IP was requested. Was a specific IP
1281:        * address requested? (host order)
1282:        */
1283: 
1284:       else if (g_state.ds_optreqip)
1285:         {
1286:           /* Yes..ACK if the requested IP address is the one already leased.
1287:            * Both addresses are in host order.
1288:            */
1289: 
1290:           if (ipaddr == g_state.ds_optreqip)
1291:             {
1292:               response = DHCPACK;
1293:             }
1294:           else
1295:             {
1296:               response = DHCPNAK;
1297:             }
1298:         }
1299: 
1300:       /* The client has specified neither a server IP nor requested
1301:        * IP address
1302:        */
1303: 
1304:       else
1305:         {
1306:           /* ACK if the IP used by the client is the one already assigned
1307:            * to it. NOTE ipaddr is in host order; ciaddr is network order!
1308:            */
1309: 
1310:           uint32_t tmp = htonl(ipaddr);
1311:           if (memcmp(&tmp, g_state.ds_inpacket.ciaddr, 4) == 0)
1312:             {
1313:               response = DHCPACK;
1314:             }
1315:           else
1316:             {
1317:               response = DHCPNAK;
1318:             }
1319:         }
1320:     }
1321: 
1322:   /* The client does not hold a lease (referenced by its MAC address) and is
1323:    * requesting a specific IP address that was, apparently, never offered to
1324:    * to the client.  Perform some sanity checks before sending the NAK.
1325:    */
1326: 
1327:   else if (g_state.ds_optreqip && !g_state.ds_optserverip)
1328:     {
1329:       ninfo("Server IP: %08" PRIx32 " Requested IP: %08" PRIx32 "\n",
1330:             (uint32_t)g_state.ds_optserverip,
1331:             (uint32_t)g_state.ds_optreqip);
1332: 
1333:       /* Is this IP address already assigned? */
1334: 
1335:       lease = dhcpd_findbyipaddr(g_state.ds_optreqip);
1336:       if (lease)
1337:         {
1338:           /* Yes.. Send NAK unless the lease has expired */
1339: 
1340:           if (!dhcpd_leaseexpired(lease))
1341:             {
1342:               response = DHCPNAK;
1343:             }
1344:         }
1345: 
1346:       /* DHCPREQUEST without DHCPDISCOVER:
1347:        * The request IP address is in the range but has not been leased,
1348:        * maybe requested before the last shutdown, lease again.
1349:        */
1350: 
1351:       else if (g_state.ds_optreqip >= g_dhcpd_config.ds_startip &&
1352:                g_state.ds_optreqip <= g_dhcpd_config.ds_endip)
1353:         {
1354:           ipaddr = g_state.ds_optreqip;
1355:           response = DHCPACK;
1356:         }
1357: 
1358:       /* The requested IP address out of range, negative */
1359: 
1360:       else
1361:         {
1362:           response = DHCPNAK;
1363:         }
1364:     }
1365: 
1366:   /* Otherwise, the client does not hold a lease and is not requesting any
1367:    * specific IP address.
1368:    */
1369: 
1370:   /* Finally, either (1) send the ACK, (2) send a NAK, or (3) remain silent
1371:    * based on the checks above.
1372:    */
1373: 
1374:   if (response == DHCPACK)
1375:     {
1376:       ninfo("ACK IP %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1377:       dhcpd_sendack(sockfd, ipaddr);
1378:     }
1379:   else if (response == DHCPNAK)
1380:     {
1381:       ninfo("NAK IP %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1382:       dhcpd_sendnak(sockfd);
1383:     }
1384:   else
1385:     {
1386:       ninfo("Remaining silent IP %08lx\n", (long)ipaddr);
1387:     }
1388: 
1389:   return OK;
1390: }

1435: /****************************************************************************
1436:  * Name: dhcpd_openlistener
1437:  ****************************************************************************/
1438: 
1439: static inline int dhcpd_openlistener(FAR const char *interface)
1440: {
1441:   struct sockaddr_in addr;
1442:   struct ifreq req;
1443:   int sockfd;
1444:   int ret;
1445: 
1446:   /* Create a socket to listen for requests from DHCP clients */
1447: 
1448:   sockfd = dhcpd_socket(interface);
1449:   if (sockfd < 0)
1450:     {
1451:       nerr("ERROR: socket failed: %d\n", errno);
1452:       return ERROR;
1453:     }
1454: 
1455:   /* Get the IP address of the selected device */
1456: 
1457:   strlcpy(req.ifr_name, interface, IFNAMSIZ);
1458:   ret = ioctl(sockfd, SIOCGIFADDR, (unsigned long)&req);
1459:   if (ret < 0)
1460:     {
1461:       nerr("ERROR: setsockopt SIOCGIFADDR failed: %d\n", errno);
1462:       close(sockfd);
1463:       return ERROR;
1464:     }
1465: 
1466:   g_state.ds_serverip = ((FAR struct sockaddr_in *)
1467:     &req.ifr_addr)->sin_addr.s_addr;
1468: 
1469:   ninfo("serverip: %08" PRIx32 "\n", ntohl(g_state.ds_serverip));
1470: 
1471:   /* Bind the socket to a local port. We have to bind to INADDRY_ANY to
1472:    * receive broadcast messages.
1473:    */
1474: 
1475:   addr.sin_family      = AF_INET;
1476:   addr.sin_port        = htons(DHCP_SERVER_PORT);
1477:   addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
1478: 
1479:   ret = bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in));
1480:   if (ret < 0)
1481:     {
1482:       nerr("ERROR: bind failed, port=%d addr=%08lx: %d\n",
1483:            addr.sin_port, (long)addr.sin_addr.s_addr, errno);
1484:       close(sockfd);
1485:       return ERROR;
1486:     }
1487: 
1488:   return sockfd;
1489: }

1570: /****************************************************************************
1571:  * Name: dhcpd_run
1572:  ****************************************************************************/
1573: 
1574: int dhcpd_run(FAR const char *interface)
1575: {
1576: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_SIGNALS
1577:   struct sigaction act;
1578: #endif
1579:   int sockfd = -1;
1580:   int nbytes;
1581: 
1582:   ninfo("Started\n");
1583: 
1584:   /* Exit if the dhcpd is already executed */
1585: 
1586:   if (g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_state == DHCPD_RUNNING)
1587:     {
1588:       return OK;
1589:     }
1590: 
1591:   /* Initialize everything to zero */
1592: 
1593:   g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_data = malloc(sizeof(struct dhcpd_state_s));
1594:   if (g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_data == NULL)
1595:     {
1596:       return -ENOMEM;
1597:     }
1598: 
1599:   memset(g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_data, 0, sizeof(struct dhcpd_state_s));
1600: 
1601:   /* Update the pid if running in daemon mode */
1602: 
1603:   g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_pid = getpid();
1604: 
1605:   /* Install signal handler for CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_SIGWAKEUP */
1606: 
1607: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_SIGNALS
1608:   memset(&act, 0, sizeof(act));
1609:   act.sa_sigaction = dhcpd_signal_handler;
1610:   act.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO;
1611:   sigaction(CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_SIGWAKEUP, &act, NULL);
1612: #endif
1613: 
1614:   /* Indicate that we have started */
1615: 
1616:   g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_state = DHCPD_RUNNING;
1617: 
1618:   /* Now loop indefinitely, reading packets from the DHCP server socket */
1619: 
1620:   while (g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_state != DHCPD_STOP_REQUESTED)
1621:     {
1622:       /* Create a socket to listen for requests from DHCP clients */
1623: 
1624:       if (sockfd < 0)
1625:         {
1626:           sockfd = dhcpd_openlistener(interface);
1627:           if (sockfd < 0)
1628:             {
1629:                 nerr("ERROR: Failed to create socket\n");
1630:                 break;
1631:             }
1632:         }
1633: 
1634:       /* Read the next g_state.ds_outpacket */
1635: 
1636:       nbytes = recv(sockfd, &g_state.ds_inpacket,
1637:                     sizeof(struct dhcpmsg_s), 0);
1638:       if (nbytes < 0)
1639:         {
1640:           /* On errors (other EINTR), close the socket and try again */
1641: 
1642:           nerr("ERROR: recv failed: %d\n", errno);
1643:           if (errno != EINTR && errno != EAGAIN)
1644:             {
1645:               close(sockfd);
1646:               sockfd = -1;
1647:             }
1648: 
1649:           continue;
1650:         }
1651: 
1652:       /* Parse the incoming message options */
1653: 
1654:       if (!dhcpd_parseoptions())
1655:         {
1656:           /* Failed to parse the message options */
1657: 
1658:           nerr("ERROR: No msg type\n");
1659:           continue;
1660:         }
1661: 
1662: #ifdef CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_HOST
1663:       /* Get the poor little uC a change to get its recvfrom in place */
1664: 
1665:       usleep(500 * 1000);
1666: #endif
1667: 
1668:       /* Now process the incoming DHCP message by its message type */
1669: 
1670:       switch (g_state.ds_optmsgtype)
1671:         {
1672:           case DHCPDISCOVER:
1673:             ninfo("DHCPDISCOVER\n");
1674:             dhcpd_discover(sockfd);
1675:             break;
1676: 
1677:           case DHCPREQUEST:
1678:             ninfo("DHCPREQUEST\n");
1679:             dhcpd_request(sockfd);
1680:             break;
1681: 
1682:           case DHCPDECLINE:
1683:             ninfo("DHCPDECLINE\n");
1684:             dhcpd_decline();
1685:             break;
1686: 
1687:           case DHCPRELEASE:
1688:             ninfo("DHCPRELEASE\n");
1689:             dhcpd_release();
1690:             break;
1691: 
1692:           case DHCPINFORM: /* Not supported */
1693:           default:
1694:             nerr("ERROR: Unsupported message type: %d\n",
1695:                  g_state.ds_optmsgtype);
1696:             break;
1697:         }
1698:     }
1699: 
1700:   free(g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_data);
1701:   g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_data = NULL;
1702:   g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_pid   = -1;
1703:   g_dhcpd_daemon.ds_state = DHCPD_STOPPED;
1704: 
1705:   return OK;
1706: }

1708: /****************************************************************************
1709:  * Name: dhcpd_start
1710:  *
1711:  * Description:
1712:  *   Start the DHCPD daemon
1713:  *
1714:  * Returned Value:
1715:  *   On success, the non-negative task ID of the DHCPDC daemon is returned;
1716:  *   On failure, a negated errno value is returned.
1717:  *
1718:  ****************************************************************************/
1719: 
1720: #ifndef CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL
1721: int dhcpd_start(FAR const char *interface)
1722: {
1723:   FAR char *argv[2];
1724:   int pid;
1725: 
1726:   argv[0] = (char *)interface;
1727:   argv[1] = NULL;
1728: 
1729:   /* Is the DHCPD in a non-running state? */
1730: 
1731:   if (dhcpd_get_pid() < 0)
1732:     {
1733:       /* Start the DHCPD daemon */
1734: 
1735:       pid = task_create("dhcpd", CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_PRIORITY,
1736:                         CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_STACKSIZE, dhcpd_task_run,
1737:                         argv);

1740:

1745:           nerr("ERROR: Failed to start the DHCPD daemon: %d\n", errval);
1746:           return -errval;
1747:         }
1748:     }
1749: 
1750:   return OK;
1751: }

1754: /****************************************************************************
1755:  * Name: dhcpd_stop
1756:  *
1757:  * Description:
1758:  *   Stop the DHCPD daemon
1759:  *
1760:  * Returned Value:
1761:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.  The current
1762:  *   implementation only returns success.
1763:  *
1764:  ****************************************************************************/
1765: 
1766: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_WAITPID
1767: int dhcpd_stop(void)
1768: {
1769:   pid_t pid;
1770: 
1771:   /* Is the DHCPD in a running state? */
1772: 
1773:   pid = dhcpd_get_pid();
1774:   if (pid >= 0)
1775:     {
1776:       /* Yes.. request that the daemon stop. */
1777: 
1778:       if (kill(pid, CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_SIGWAKEUP) < 0)
1779:         {
1780:           nerr("ERROR: kill pid %d failed: %d\n", pid, errno);

1782:         }
1783: 
1784:       /* Wait for the DHCPD client to respond to the stop request */
1785: 
1786:       if (waitpid(pid, NULL, 0) < 0)
1787:         {
1788:           nerr("ERROR: waitpid failed: %d\n", errno);
1789:           return -errno;
1790:         }
1791:     }
1792: 
1793:   return OK;
1794: }

47: /****************************************************************************
48:  * Name: up_create_stack
49:  *
50:  * Description:
51:  *   Allocate a stack for a new thread and setup up stack-related information
52:  *   in the TCB.
53:  *
54:  *   The following TCB fields must be initialized by this function:
55:  *
56:  *   - adj_stack_size: Stack size after adjustment for hardware, processor,
57:  *     etc.  This value is retained only for debug purposes.
58:  *   - stack_alloc_ptr: Pointer to allocated stack
59:  *   - stack_base_ptr: Adjusted stack base pointer after the TLS Data and
60:  *     Arguments has been removed from the stack allocation.
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   - tcb: The TCB of new task
64:  *   - stack_size:  The requested stack size.  At least this much
65:  *     must be allocated.
66:  *   - ttype:  The thread type.  This may be one of following (defined in
67:  *     include/nuttx/sched.h):
68:  *
69:  *       TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_TASK     Normal user task
70:  *       TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD  User pthread
71:  *       TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL   Kernel thread
72:  *
73:  *     This thread type is normally available in the flags field of the TCB,
74:  *     however, there are certain contexts where the TCB may not be fully
75:  *     initialized when up_create_stack is called.
76:  *
77:  *     If either CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED or CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL are defined,
78:  *     then this thread type may affect how the stack is allocated.  For
79:  *     example, kernel thread stacks should be allocated from protected
80:  *     kernel memory.  Stacks for user tasks and threads must come from
81:  *     memory that is accessible to user code.
82:  *
83:  ****************************************************************************/
84: 
85: int up_create_stack(struct tcb_s *tcb, size_t stack_size, int ttype)
86: {
87: #ifdef CONFIG_TLS_ALIGNED
88:   size_t alignment = TLS_STACK_ALIGN;
89: 
90:   /* The allocated stack size must not exceed the maximum possible for the
91:    * TLS feature.
92:    */
93: 
94:   DEBUGASSERT(stack_size <= TLS_MAXSTACK);
95:   if (stack_size > TLS_MAXSTACK)
96:     {
97:       stack_size = TLS_MAXSTACK;
98:     }
99: #elif CONFIG_STACK_ALIGN_SIZE > 0
100:   size_t alignment = CONFIG_STACK_ALIGN_SIZE;
101: #endif
102: 
103:   /* Is there already a stack allocated of a different size? */
104: 
105:   if (tcb->stack_alloc_ptr && tcb->adj_stack_size != stack_size)
106:     {
107:       /* Yes.. Release the old stack */
108: 
109:       up_release_stack(tcb, ttype);
110:     }
111: 
112:   /* Do we need to allocate a new stack? */
113: 
114:   if (!tcb->stack_alloc_ptr)
115:     {
116:       /* Allocate the stack.  If DEBUG is enabled (but not stack debug),
117:        * then create a zeroed stack to make stack dumps easier to trace.
118:        * If TLS is enabled, then we must allocate aligned stacks.
119:        */
120: 
121:        tcb->stack_alloc_ptr =
122: #if defined(CONFIG_TLS_ALIGNED) || (CONFIG_STACK_ALIGN_SIZE > 0)
123:         group_memalign(tcb->group, alignment, stack_size);
124: #else /* CONFIG_TLS_ALIGNED || CONFIG_STACK_ALIGN_SIZE > 0 */
125:         group_malloc(tcb->group, stack_size);
126: #endif /* CONFIG_TLS_ALIGNED */
127: 
128: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
129:       /* Was the allocation successful? */
130: 
131:       if (!tcb->stack_alloc_ptr)
132:         {
133:           serr("ERROR: Failed to allocate stack, size %zu\n", stack_size);
134:         }
135: #endif
136:     }
137: 
138:   /* Did we successfully allocate a stack? */
139: 
140:   if (tcb->stack_alloc_ptr)
141:     {
142:       uintptr_t top_of_stack;
143:       size_t size_of_stack;
144: 
145:       /* The ARM uses a "full descending" stack:
146:        * the stack grows toward lower addresses in memory.
147:        * The stack pointer register points to the last pushed item in
148:        * the stack.
149:        * Items on the stack are referenced as positive word offsets from sp.
150:        */
151: 
152:       top_of_stack = (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_alloc_ptr + stack_size;
153: 
154:       /* Align the top of stack to STACK_ALIGNMENT. */
155: 
156:       top_of_stack  = STACKFRAME_ALIGN_DOWN(top_of_stack);
157:       size_of_stack = top_of_stack - (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
158: 
159:       /* Save the adjusted stack values in the struct tcb_s */
160: 
161:       tcb->stack_base_ptr = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
162:       tcb->adj_stack_size = size_of_stack;
163: 
164: #ifdef CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION
165:       /* If stack debug is enabled, then fill the stack with a
166:        * recognizable value that we can use later to test for high
167:        * water marks.
168:        */
169: 
170:       arm_stack_color(tcb->stack_base_ptr, tcb->adj_stack_size);
171: #endif /* CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION */
172:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_FREE_STACK);
173: 
174:       board_autoled_on(LED_STACKCREATED);
175:       return OK;
176:     }
177: 
178:   return ERROR;
179: }

74: {

76:          ((uint32_t)buf[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)buf[3] << 24);

92:                      const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
93: {

95:   size_t psk_len;
96:   size_t api_len;
97:   int ret;

99:   if (buf == NULL || cred == NULL)
100:     {

102:     }

104:   if (buflen < VP_RECORD_SIZE)
105:     {
106:       return -E2BIG;

109:   ret = vp_credentials_validate(cred);

117:   api_len  = vp_len(cred->api_key, sizeof(cred->api_key));

119:   memset(buf, 0, VP_RECORD_SIZE);

122:   vp_put16(buf + VP_OFF_FLAGS,

126:   buf[VP_OFF_PSK_LEN]  = (uint8_t)psk_len;

128:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_PSK, cred->password, psk_len);
129:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_API, cred->api_key, api_len);
130:   vp_put32(buf + VP_OFF_CRC, vp_crc32(buf, VP_RECORD_SIZE - 4));
131:   return VP_RECORD_SIZE;

136: {

139:   for (i = used; i < field; i++)

150: int vp_record_decode(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len,
151:                      struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
152: {
153:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s parsed;
154:   size_t ssid_len;
155:   size_t psk_len;
156:   size_t api_len;
157:   uint16_t flags;
158: 
159:   if (buf == NULL || cred == NULL)
160:     {
161:       return -EINVAL;
162:     }
163: 
164:   /* Exactly one size is legal.  A shorter file is a truncated write and a
165:    * longer one is not this format, and neither is worth guessing about.
166:    */
167: 
168:   if (len != VP_RECORD_SIZE)
169:     {
170:       return -EBADMSG;
171:     }
172: 
173:   if (memcmp(buf + VP_OFF_MAGIC, VP_RECORD_MAGIC, 4) != 0 ||
174:       vp_get16(buf + VP_OFF_VERSION) != VP_RECORD_VERSION ||
175:       buf[VP_OFF_RESERVED] != 0)
176:     {
177:       return -EBADMSG;
178:     }
179: 
180:   if (vp_get32(buf + VP_OFF_CRC) != vp_crc32(buf, VP_RECORD_SIZE - 4))
181:     {
182:       return -EBADMSG;
183:     }
184: 
185:   flags    = vp_get16(buf + VP_OFF_FLAGS);
186:   ssid_len = buf[VP_OFF_SSID_LEN];
187:   psk_len  = buf[VP_OFF_PSK_LEN];
188:   api_len  = vp_len((const char *)(buf + VP_OFF_API),
189:                     VELASIGHT_PROV_API_KEY_MAX);
190: 
191:   if ((flags & ~(uint16_t)VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN) != 0)
192:     {
193:       return -EBADMSG;
194:     }
195: 
196:   if (ssid_len == 0 || ssid_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX)
197:     {
198:       return -EBADMSG;
199:     }
200: 
201:   if (psk_len != 0 &&
202:       (psk_len < VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MIN || psk_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX))
203:     {
204:       return -EBADMSG;
205:     }
206: 
207:   if (((flags & VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN) != 0) != (psk_len == 0))
208:     {
209:       return -EBADMSG;
210:     }
211: 
212:   if (!vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_SSID, ssid_len,
213:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX) ||
214:       !vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_PSK, psk_len,
215:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX))
216:     {
217:       return -EBADMSG;
218:     }
219: 
220:   if (api_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_API_KEY_MAX ||
221:       !vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_API, api_len,
222:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_API_KEY_MAX))
223:     {
224:       return -EBADMSG;
225:     }
226: 
227:   memset(&parsed, 0, sizeof(parsed));
228:   memcpy(parsed.ssid, buf + VP_OFF_SSID, ssid_len);
229:   memcpy(parsed.password, buf + VP_OFF_PSK, psk_len);
230:   memcpy(parsed.api_key, buf + VP_OFF_API, api_len);
231:   parsed.generation   = vp_get32(buf + VP_OFF_GEN);
232:   parsed.open_network = psk_len == 0;
233: 
234:   /* The record can be structurally perfect and still describe credentials the
235:    * running code would refuse, for instance after a limit changes.  Treat that
236:    * as corrupt rather than handing the caller something it cannot use.
237:    */
238: 
239:   if (vp_credentials_validate(&parsed) < 0)
240:     {
241:       return -EBADMSG;
242:     }
243: 
244:   *cred = parsed;
245:   return 0;

301: int vp_store_save(const char *path,
302:                   const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
303: {
304:   uint8_t record[VP_RECORD_SIZE];
305:   char tmp[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX + 16];
306:   FILE *stream;
307:   int ret;
308: 
309:   if (path == NULL || cred == NULL)
310:     {
311:       return -EINVAL;
312:     }
313: 
314:   if (strlen(path) >= VP_STORE_PATH_MAX)
315:     {
316:       return -ENAMETOOLONG;
317:     }
318: 
319:   ret = vp_record_encode(record, sizeof(record), cred);
320:   if (ret < 0)
321:     {
322:       return ret;
323:     }
324: 
325:   ret = vp_make_parent(path);
326:   if (ret < 0)
327:     {
328:       return ret;
329:     }
330: 
331:   ret = vp_store_temp_path(path, tmp, sizeof(tmp));
332:   if (ret < 0)
333:     {
334:       return ret;
335:     }
336: 
337:   stream = fopen(tmp, "wb");
338:   if (stream == NULL)
339:     {
340:       return -errno;
341:     }
342: 
343:   /* Write, flush, fsync, close, rename.  Without the fsync the rename can be
344:    * durable while the data behind it is not, which on a power cut leaves a
345:    * record that passes its own CRC check by accident or fails it for no
346:    * reason the next boot can explain.
347:    */
348: 
349:   if (fwrite(record, 1, sizeof(record), stream) != sizeof(record) ||
350:       fflush(stream) != 0 || fsync(fileno(stream)) != 0)
351:     {
352:       ret = errno != 0 ? -errno : -EIO;
353:       fclose(stream);
354:       unlink(tmp);
355:       return ret;
356:     }
357: 
358:   if (fclose(stream) != 0)
359:     {
360:       ret = errno != 0 ? -errno : -EIO;
361:       unlink(tmp);
362:       return ret;
363:     }
364: 
365:   if (rename(tmp, path) < 0)
366:     {
367:       ret = -errno;
368:       /* Keep a complete, fsynced scratch record.  FAT replacement unlinks an
369:        * existing destination before rename, so this may be the only valid
370:        * copy left after an interrupted replacement.  load() recovers it when
371:        * the final path is absent.
372:        */
373:       return ret;
374:     }
375: 
376:   sync();
377:   return 0;
378: }

380: int vp_store_load(const char *path,
381:                   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
382: {
383:   uint8_t record[VP_RECORD_SIZE + 1];
384:   char tmp[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX + 16];
385:   FILE *stream;
386:   size_t nread;
387:   bool recover = false;
388: 
389:   if (path == NULL || cred == NULL)
390:     {
391:       return -EINVAL;
392:     }
393: 
394:   stream = fopen(path, "rb");
395:   if (stream == NULL)
396:     {
397:       /* ENOTDIR belongs with ENOENT here: a directory component that is
398:        * missing, or is a file, means nothing was ever stored.  NuttX's FAT
399:        * reports ENOTDIR for the missing-directory case where Linux reports
400:        * ENOENT, and a device that has simply never been provisioned should
401:        * not look like a broken one.  EINVAL is deliberately left alone: on
402:        * that filesystem it means the configured path cannot be represented,
403:        * which is a misconfiguration worth seeing.
404:        */
405: 
406:       if (errno == ENOENT || errno == ENOTDIR)
407:         {
408:           if (vp_store_temp_path(path, tmp, sizeof(tmp)) < 0)
409:             {
410:               return -ENOENT;
411:             }
412: 
413:           stream = fopen(tmp, "rb");
414:           if (stream == NULL)
415:             {
416:               return errno == ENOENT || errno == ENOTDIR ? -ENOENT : -errno;
417:             }
418: 
419:           recover = true;
420:         }
421:       else
422:         {
423:           return -errno;
424:         }
425:     }
426: 
427:   nread = fread(record, 1, sizeof(record), stream);
428:   fclose(stream);
429: 
430:   if (vp_record_decode(record, nread, cred) < 0)
431:     {
432:       return -EBADMSG;
433:     }
434: 
435:   if (recover)
436:     {
437:       if (rename(tmp, path) < 0)
438:         {
439:           return -errno;
440:         }
441: 
442:       sync();
443:     }
444: 
445:   return 0;
446: }
